chapters.title: Chapter 201: Overwhelming Talent
paragraphs: There was an explosion, and so what?
Although it was unexpected, it wasn’t like they were about to stop the battle. Not even in the slightest.
Kent had just gotten into the battle, and the Saintess was also enjoying it. Though she hadn’t recognized it yet, she was starting to like Kent more and more as they fought.
Their friendship meter had already risen to 10%, and as the battle progressed, it began to climb even higher as Kent and she clashed more fiercely.
A flaming lion flashed out of Kent’s sword and sped toward the Saintess, who swung her spear, sending out a powerful wind arc that obliterated the lion.
Three more lions followed as Kent unleashed another three strikes. These lions were much larger and fiercer as he continued using the [Elemental Manipulation] skill he had received from Lilian.
"Wind Bees!"

The Saintess unleashed a powerful attack that immediately filled the air with the buzzing sound of bees. They buzzed as they sped toward Kent, who suddenly found himself facing hundreds of wind arcs buzzing at him.
’Damn... this is troublesome.’
Kent didn’t wait around and unleashed a counter.
"Rapid Slash!"
This was the first form of the [Annihilation Sword] he had gotten from Vexthra. It had seven forms, and the first form was [Rapid Slash.]

This was the best counter for him, as just a single swing was enough to unleash countless sword arcs, almost like the wind arcs coming at him. He managed to unleash the attack twice, releasing hundreds of sword arcs.

But they weren’t enough to stop the bees, forcing him to use his Blink to escape. However, just as he did, he came within the line of sight of the Saintess, who moved like the wind and thrust her spear at Kent’s neck.
"Really?"

Kent parried the stab and kicked forward, but the Saintess caught his leg and tossed him into the air. She jumped up and landed a powerful kick to his stomach, sending him flying toward the ground. However, the Saintess wasn’t done.
She appeared on the ground where Kent was about to land, ready to strike him again.
However, before she could attach again, she was forced to step back when lightning suddenly surged out of Kent’s body, shooting toward the Saintess.
"Wait a minute, you have dual elemental affinity?" she asked, staring at the lightning now dancing around Kent.
"What can I say? I’m just that awesome," Kent smiled. "Now face my lightning!"
Golden lightning danced around him, leaving a trail behind as he sped toward the Saintess with a much faster stride.
"...Unbelievable"
The Saintess muttered as a powerful strike from Kent pushed her back. More attacks followed, with Kent switching between skills and techniques.
The Saintess, too, was the same.

Kent didn’t have the upper hand, but he also wasn’t at too much of a disadvantage as they battled. In a way, the Saintess’s main objective, which was to torture him, changed when she sensed his talent.

Kent was just too talented, and as someone who was also considered a genius with the spear, she began to like him more and more as they fought. Kent was also thrilled, despite knowing he wasn’t her match... not just yet.

Gaia had analyzed the Saintess and told him she was only using 70% of her strength and skills below the Heaven grade to attack. Kent wasn’t disappointed. He knew she was doing this to keep the fight going.
In that case, Kent was thrilled and started measuring his skills and honing them to the stage he could currently handle.
But even after 30 minutes of using the Annihilation Sword technique, he still hadn’t reached the true form of even the first form. This meant he wouldn’t be able to start mastering the second form.
He managed to achieve 100 sword arcs from a single rapid slash. But even that wasn’t enough to measure the true form of the technique.
In fact, he was far from reaching that stage, which begs the question of just how monstrous the technique was and how much he had to put into it just to reach its true form.

Kent had to switch to a new technique, which is the [Nine Calamities Sword Strike]. This technique came from the sword sheath, and at the moment, he was only at the [True Despair Sword Strike], which is the first form.
This one, too, was much more complex than he had expected. The Saintess, who raised her strength to 70% the moment he started using it, shows just how dangerous the skill is.

He used this one for a couple of minutes and then stopped. Unlike the [Rapid Slash], which he managed to utilize in countering the wind arcs, the [True Despair Sword Strike] was much more suited for killing.
Kent switched back to elemental manipulation, and for another 30 minutes, he went through it gradually until he decided to unleash the true, current form of the skill.
"Elemental Lord."
Kent swung his weapon, and a large, pointed sword made purely of fire erupted from his sword, shooting toward the Saintess, who immediately sensed danger.
The attack was just like when Kent unleashed the 72-String Sovereign Strike. It was his first time using it and also his first time forming a sword from his flame element.
The spear arrived in front of the Saintess, who immediately unleashed a powerful Heaven-grade skill just to counter.
"Heaven-Piercing Spear!"
She stabbed her spear forward, and a powerful, colossal form of the spear appeared, colliding with the flaming spear.
BOOM
The attacks exploded, and both the Saintess and Kent were sent flying. They each coughed up a mouthful of blood, but in the next second, they clashed again.
Ingrid was watching all this with a shocked expression. She knew deep within her heart that she wasn’t Kent’s match—not even in the slightest.
She couldn’t last even 30 minutes when she sparred with her master. Yet Kent was going on for hours already. That is just monstrous.

Four hours later, Kent was sent flying back, landing on the ground with a heavy thud, and passed out. He was spent, but he had forced the Saintess to use 75% of her strength, which was a great achievement on his part.
Saintess Neomi walked to his passed-out body, picked him up in a princess carry, and took him to a room to rest. She was pleased with Kent’s performance.
All those who saw it were shocked.
Gate Master Mara and Gate Master Camilla were present, along with some elders and others who had watched the battle from a distance.
Of course, none of them realized this battle had brought the Sect Master, who had been in seclusion for 10 years, out.
When Kent unleashed his aura, the Sect Master sensed it, and despite his seclusion, he emerged to see who could unleash such a terrifying aura.

He thought a divine being had descended for a moment, but when he saw Kent, he was forced to raise an eyebrow. As a peak Root Ascension cultivator, he could somewhat sense the nature of the sword’s intent, qi, and aura.
Then, he witnessed Kent’s four-hour battle with the Saintess, and in that moment, he saw a way out—a future for the Sword Gate and the sect as a whole.

After returning to his residence, he immediately called a meeting with the Spear and Sword Gate Masters. Since they had witnessed Kent’s battle, he wanted them to take the lead on what he had in mind.
Kent, however, was passed out for ten hours. When he woke up, he saw his master sitting beside him, wiping his naked body with a wet towel...
"So I lost, huh?" Kent muttered, but a smile played on his lips...

chapters.title: Chapter 202: Evil Intent
paragraphs: Kent woke up with a refreshed vigour and strength. Though his body was practically wrecked, the situation he woke up in was encouraging, so he didn’t scream in pain.
Saintess Selene was cleaning his body with a wet towel.
"Do you now understand what it takes to become a Saint or Saintess with the spear?" The first thing Selene said was to address what Kent was thinking about.
She is a Saintess, just like her sister, Saintess Neomi, but she wouldn’t even be able to win a duel against her. In fact, many Saints and Saintesses would lose to Neomi.
She is a monster...just like how many now describe Kent.
"She is strong, no doubt. But I will be able to defeat her in under a year," Kent said, knowing a year on the outside is 24 years in the tower. He will become a monster by then.
"You might want to handle your internal injuries first," Saintess Selene said as she finished cleaning him. Kent dressed and chose to go outside with his master.
"Where is your sister?" Kent asked as they sat down under a tree.

"She is in seclusion. After your battle, it seems she has gained some form of enlightenment, so she immediately entered seclusion. As for Ingrid, she has gone to listen to a teaching from one of her favorite instructors."
"I see," Kent nodded.
Gaia had already told him about enlightenment, so he knew that whatever the Saintess was going through would likely benefit her greatly.
"Then what are you doing here? I doubt you just came to clean my sweaty body," Kent asked, looking straight into her eyes.
Saintess Selene simply smiled and stood up.

"Unity has a duel later today. He tried reaching you to tell you, but you were unconscious. So, when I heard from Ingrid that big sister had beaten you unconscious, I came to check up on you and inform you," the Saintess laughed.
"She didn’t beat me up. We fought for four hours, and I lost. She didn’t beat me up, per se," Kent replied, but the Saintess just smiled.
"If you say so," she smirked, making Kent grit his teeth.
[She got you real good, master.] Gaia also fanned the flames.
’Shut up, Gaia...Whose side are you on, anyway?’
[I am on your side, master...but sometimes, the truth hurts,] Gaia giggled, making Kent want to smack her silly. He closed his eyes and meditated by replaying the battle in his head.
The Saintess giggled and left. She was headed to the Archer Gate, where her sister was gearing up for a duel. Kent would go there, but only when it was almost time for the duel.
As for now...He needed to evaluate the battle and figure out his shortcomings.
Meanwhile, in a certain room in the sect, the Sect Master, by the name of Gideon, could be seen sitting facing Gate Master Camilla and Gate Master Mara.
"You two already know why I called you here... so why don’t we get down to it," Sect Master Gideon said to the two ladies.
"What can you tell me about that young man who had the duel with the Spear Saintess?"
The two ladies stared at each other for a few seconds before Gate Master Mara chose to speak up.

"His name is Kent Madson. He is the disciple of my previous disciple, the Sword Saintess. He arrived in the sect less than a week ago but has already caused too much trouble. I am afraid the other gate might be making a move on him soon."
"But aside from his troubles, he is also a very talented swordsman with all three main aspects of a swordsman awakened."
The Sect Master nodded.
He had witnessed the duel between Kent and the Spear Saintess, and he could tell from their clash that Kent indeed possessed all three aspects—the intent, qi, and body.
"Do you know anything about his background?" Sect Master Gideon asked.
"No. However, I am sure he is from a very influential background, considering he was able to purchase a platinum membership at the Tasty Home Pavilion," Gate Master Mara answered.

Sect Master Gideon raised an eyebrow upon hearing that. The amount Kent spent was something that could be used to purchase a couple of cultivation resources, and there would still be some change to spare.

"Then it’s safe to assume he has a very rich background. However, he is also a disciple of this sect, so he falls under our jurisdiction. That said, what do you two ladies think of him?" the Sect Master asked.

He had seen the two Gate Masters watching the battle from afar, so he knew their interest in Kent was not something to dismiss. They were clearly interested in him, so they had been observing the duel to learn more about him.
"I just want to smack him silly for traumatizing two of my disciples," Gate Master Mara said with a straight face.

"I just want to know him more and, if possible, form an alliance with him. That brat is quite capable, and having a good relationship with him will be much more beneficial than being his enemy," Gate Master Camilla added.
’Bunch of liars,’ the Sect Master smirked inwardly.

Who were they trying to fool? He could tell they were lying, but he didn’t care. At least there was no malicious intent from them, so he could only assume they wanted something more personal with him than they weren’t willing to share with him.

"Since that is the case, I won’t interfere in your affairs. However, this talent is rare and must be protected. It’s been a long time since such a monster appeared on this continent, and while we know nothing about him, it’s safe to say he is someone we can bet on.

"I happened to sense something profound from him, and if my assumptions are correct, this kid is someone who can help all of us greatly," the Sect Master said, making the two Gate Masters look at him with an attentive gaze.
"What do you want us to do, Sect Master?" Gate Master Camilla asked.

"I want you two to protect him from the others. I have been in seclusion for almost a decade, but I can tell what has been going on inside the sect. A rot is spreading, and the others will try to pull him down.
So don’t let them succeed. I am close to a breakthrough, so for now, you two are to ensure he is always protected. You can use any means necessary to enforce this... but just make sure he is safe.
In a year’s time, I will be out, and then, hopefully, he will become someone strong enough to handle what I have in store for him," the Sect Master said, and the two ladies could only nod.
They may be sitting and talking with the Sect Master now, but they know the kind of person he is and what he would do to get what he wants.
The two knew Kent had just entered serious trouble the moment this old dog had set his sights on him.
As such, the two ladies, who understood what this entailed, had made a vow never to let the Sect Master succeed. This meant all animosity against Kent was scrapped.
Though the Sword Gate Master wanted to torture Kent, she also wouldn’t want the only disciple of her most cherished disciple to fall into evil’s hands.

chapters.title: Chapter 203: Sight of Evil
paragraphs: Twenty years ago, Gate Master Camilla took in a disciple she met on one of her missions outside the sect. It was similar to how Saintess Selene met Kent.
However, while the Saintess and Kent fought over a sword sheath, Gate Master Camilla and her disciple, Zaila, clashed over a misunderstanding and a sense of duty...
Back then, Zaila was a mercenary hired to guard a certain overprivileged heir of a noble family who had come to the Athea Kingdom for sightseeing.

Although Zaila hated the job, she had to feed herself and buy cultivation resources, so she chose to take on the well-paying task. Her only responsibility was to ensure the one she was guarding had a good time.
Unfortunately, while they were browsing through some stores in Vastport City, the young master spotted a certain necklace he wanted to buy for one of his many girlfriends.

Unfortunately for him, before he could make his move, Gate Master Camilla took the necklace and paid for it. This didn’t sit well with the young master, so he chose to walk the path of arrogance and immediately resorted to insults.
Unfortunately for him, Gate Master Camilla was a no-nonsense kind of gal, so she didn’t let him have his way. A single slap knocked out nearly all his teeth and left him unconscious.
This forced Zaila to step in, as it was her job to protect the heir. Despite her weaker cultivation base, she and the Gate Master clashed in a fierce fight.
Through the battle, the Gate Master noticed her talent and offered her a much better opportunity, which Zaila accepted. This led to her becoming a disciple of one of the strongest women in the world.
She began studying under her, honing her skills, and gradually gained recognition within the sect.
Over time, her fame spread throughout the sect, and just like Kent, she became a monster many wanted to challenge, though none succeeded.
This continued for six years until, one day, the Sect Master set his sights on her.
Back then, when the Sect Master decided to make Zaila someone the sect could rely on, the Gate Master of the Spear Gate was overjoyed.
In fact, she was so happy that she failed to heed the advice of the Sword Gate Master, who had been a Gate Master longer than her.
She only wanted what was best for her disciple and decided for Zaila to undergo more rigorous training under the Sect Master.
For four years, Zaila traveled with the Sect Master, going on missions, entering secret domains, and much more.
However, the moment of reckoning came ten years ago when Zaila went on a mission and never returned. Her life shattered, and the most talented and genius disciple was gone just like that.
This broke Gate Master Camilla to the point that for an entire year, she locked herself away and could do nothing but cry her heart out.
She just couldn’t understand what had happened. Zaila died on a Very High-ranked mission, yet she had survived dozens of calamity-ranked missions. It made no sense.
So, after a year of grieving, she began to investigate. However, no matter where she looked, she found no evidence. Eventually, she turned to the Sword Gate Master, who was happy to help.
Through her, Gate Master Camilla learned of similar cases where genius disciples had died under strange circumstances. After connecting the dots, everything pointed to the Sect Master.
They began investigating him, and though it was dangerous, the two women played their cards carefully.
Over the past ten years, while the Sect Master was in seclusion, they gathered enough evidence. After analyzing everything, they concluded.
They concluded that the Sect Master was an evil practitioner.

Evil practitioners do not follow the orthodox path of cultivation. Instead, they steal from talented cultivators through dangerous and malevolent rituals, which often result in the death of those they exploit.

Though not yet confirmed, this discovery was the only conclusion they could reach. The two women didn’t want to act without having all the facts, so on the surface, they continued their roles as Gate Masters.
In the background, however, they worked tirelessly to uncover the truth.
They aimed to understand what was happening and, if possible, put an end to it.
So they bided their time, waiting for the right moment until the Sect Master called them to discuss Kent.
Through the talk, Gate Master Camilla, who may have just gotten an answer to her disciple’s death, wanted to erupt. Luckily, Gate Master Mara kept her in check.
⟦I happened to sense something profound from him, and if my assumptions are correct, this kid is someone who can help all of us greatly.⟧
That was exactly what the sect master said to her years ago before she handed over her disciple to him, and now, he said the same thing about Kent. It was the last straw that broke the camel’s back.
But now that they had their answer, the two ladies would do everything in their power to avenge those they had lost.
The Sword Gate Master hadn’t said anything about why he was doing this, but one doesn’t need a genie to know she, too, may have undergone a misfortune with the Sect Master.
Unbeknownst to them, while they were busy with what had to happen next, the Sect Master also began making his plans.

When they left to devise a plan on how to move forward with this discovery, the Sect Master arrived in an underground cave where thick red chains, slick with blood, could be seen connected to a large cauldron holding it in place
Blood and some human and monster body parts filled the cauldron.
He walked past the cauldron and stopped in front of another cave. The moment he entered, a sinister smile appeared on his face.
He was face to face with two cages. Inside one of the cages was Zaila, the disciple of the Spear Gate Master, who was supposed to have died ten years ago. She was still alive—barely.
But she was breathing, and connected to her neck was a chain tube that led to the cauldron. She was acting as a blood bank.
Inside the other cage was a green-haired beauty who still maintained her beauty and poise despite being locked up for over six decades. Just like Zaila, she also acts as a blood bank.

The Sect Master stopped in front of Zaila’s cage and spoke, "It seems your master still misses you and even seems to suspect me... though I am not sure just yet." He walked around the cage and came to the front again.

"Though she doesn’t have your kind of talent, she will make do with her blood. If next I sense her suspicion, I might just consider bringing her here and making you watch her die." The Sect Master laughed before walking away, glancing at the green-haired beauty seated with her eyes closed.
Zaila clenched her fist while gritting her teeth. In fact, the gritting was loud enough to force the green-haired beauty to open her eyes and sigh.
The two are like misfortune sisters down in the dark cave...
’Little sister, I hope you are living a much better life than I am at the moment.’ A smile appeared on her face, and the image of a certain Sword Gate Master appeared in her head.
Yes... this was Nara, the older sister of Sword Gate Master Mara, who had gone missing 67 years ago while she was a core disciple of the Divine Palace Sect.
It was also the reason why Gate Master Mara joined the sect and began investigating the Sect Master.
’I only wish one day I will be able to see you again,’ Nara said before closing her eyes again.
Meanwhile, far from the sect, Uncle Drew, who was getting ready to kidnap a certain brat, closed his eyes and muttered something.
A few seconds later, a name appeared in his mind, along with where to go next—to bring the fourth member into the Night Riders.

chapters.title: Chapter 204: The Kidnapping Game
paragraphs: Somewhere in the Varyndor Kingdom...
Uncle Drew and Saden, whom Kent had tasked with capturing and delivering Turyn, the heir of the Miller family, had finally begun making plans to carry out the mission.
They had arrived in the Varyndor Kingdom days ago but hadn’t immediately gotten to work.

They might be the Night Riders, but they still had to be cautious. They first started gathering intel on their target, and after three days of back-and-forth, they finally met to devise a concrete plan.
Inside a private room in a certain inn, Uncle Drew and Saden sat over a drink. Though they weren’t drinking, they also weren’t talking.
However, they were talking—just not out loud. It was all happening telepathically. Just like Kent had with his women, the Night Riders also shared the same connection with each other and with Kent.
"I discovered that the target will be leaving for Althea Kingdom tomorrow. He will travel with ten Root Saints, five Root Sages, and two Root Great Sages in his entourage.
Aside from them, there will be three female servants who will be serving him directly," Saden said, reporting what she had observed after spying on the Miller family for the past three days.
"The young master was right," Uncle Drew said. Before leaving, Kent had told him there was a high chance Turyn would travel to the Althea Kingdom.

It’s the annual auction, where some of the most valuable goods will be sold over a span of seven days, with each blessed day auctioning great treasures that can make or break anyone... even an entire kingdom.
Naturally, people like Turyn, who are rich, would try their luck in the chaotic bidding war that can go on for hours.

Because of this, Kent predicted Turyn would be coming to Althea Kingdom and advised Uncle Drew to ambush him on the road. Of course, since there are no teleportation gates connecting the kingdoms, they will spend some time on the road.
"Then this will be easy enough," Saden said.
"Indeed. Let’s wait for them at the most suitable spot," Uncle Drew said through telepathy. After fine-tuning some details in the next couple of seconds, they left.
A day later, a lavish carriage left the Miller Mansion and started heading toward Althea Kingdom. Within this carriage was Turyn, the heir of the Miller family.
Turyn was a genius core disciple in the Varyndor Royal Sect. He was one of the many geniuses the kingdom had to offer. However, while he may have been the apple of everyone’s eye...
He was, in fact, a scum who deserved a whole lot of torture before being put down.

He had hurt many innocent women, with Manager Alina being one of them. What she had been through was traumatizing enough that her passion for something was blocked, and she couldn’t let go of the past even after decades.
Of course, it wasn’t as if his family was unaware of his actions. There had been many reports, but they chose to silence the victims.

However, as they say, what goes around comes around... It seems Turyn’s day has come back to haunt him. Of course, he had no idea this danger was looming over him. He could only wait for what was coming.
Hours after leaving Varyndor Kingdom, night fell, and they had to camp before continuing their journey the next morning.
"Young Master Turyn, there is a suitable place just a few kilometers from here. We will camp there," one of the Root Sages said to Turyn, who was playing with the three mages inside the carriage.
"Okay..." he said, not even bothering to ask for further details. So they left, and a couple of kilometers later, they arrived at an area with lush greenery and trees for cover.
It was the ideal place where most travelers camped for the night. They quickly set up tents, and just like that, they began waiting for nightfall.
However, while they remained on high alert, a few meters away, three hooded figures—one with two swords on their back and another with a bow and arrow—continued to observe the travelers.
"Remember, don’t kill the others... We are only after the one inside the tent with the three ladies. I will handle the Root Great Sages and the Root Sages. You should handle the Root Saints and him,"
Uncle Drew said to Saden before he moved.
Saden also moved, knowing she was after the main package. All he had to do was press a talisman against Turyn’s forehead while he was passed out, and he would be transported to the Tower Prison.
They moved.
Uncle Drew made his way, using the night to his advantage. He activated [Veil of Death], rendering himself invisible to the living.
Inside one of the three tents built, one of the Root Great Sages was seated in a lotus posture, while the first stood guard outside a couple of meters away.
He slipped inside, and before the Root Great Sage could sense anything, a kick landed on the back of his head, knocking him out cold.
Uncle Drew didn’t waste any time and immediately moved to his next target. The second Root Great Sage, who was also unaware of the lurking danger, felt a kick land on the back of his head.
He fell back, but before he could hit the ground, a shadowy mist appeared around him, and in the next second, he was inside the tent with the first Root Great Sage.
Saden passed by Uncle Drew right after he took down the Root Great Sage. She moved closer to the tent housing five Saints.
Five were patrolling outside. She entered and, using a skill called [Rider’s Night Clone], split into five and executed a combined attack that knocked them out simultaneously.
The four clones were made of the energy of the night. It was the type of skill that could be used only at night...
The attack demanded precision, and she delivered it perfectly. The night worked in her favor, allowing her to avoid overexerting herself.
By the time she was done caring for the five Saints, Uncle Drew had also finished dealing with three Sages, leaving only two.

The two were far from the five remaining Root Saints, so she repeated the attacks using the clones. Just like that, after Uncle Drew delivered the blow to the last two Root Sages, the only ones left were the Heir and the three ladies with him.
Uncle Drew gave Saden the go-ahead since he wanted her to have this one.
She moved and entered the tent, dismissing the Veil when he was right in front of Turyn. He was in bed with one of the three ladies, so he was caught off guard.
He pulled out and was about to reach for his weapon when one of the ladies beside him, who had been sucking his dick just a couple of minutes ago, delivered a punch to his face, knocking him out.
"...Punk."
Her hand hurt, but she was satisfied with the punch.
She spat on him, making Saden look at her strangely. "Please don’t kill us, we are doing this against our will," the lady said.
It was hard not to give her credit; she was a survivor. She knew when to use a situation to her advantage. So, while Saden would likely have wiped their memories of the incident, she chose not to.

Instead, he walked to one side of the room and retrieved something from a box. "This will be enough to change your lives." It was a space ring containing all the money Turyn was going to spend during the auction.
She gave it to the bold lady, and then, retrieving the talisman, he placed it on his forehead and was sucked away by an unknown force.
Just like that, word would soon reach the Miller Noble family about the disappearance of their son and all his wealth.

The three ladies also traveled to the Eldorath Kingdom, a small city where they changed their identities and started a new life, free from the torture they had endured at the hands of the Miller family.
Chaos was about to ensue...

chapters.title: Chapter 205: Quests Completed
paragraphs: A few hours before the kidnapping game, Kent had passed out after he got his ass handed to him by the Spear Saintess.

Though he wasn’t calling it a beating and more like a duel where he lost, in the end, he passed out and had to spend 10 hours in dreamland, knowing nothing of the mischief his two-night riders were up to.
But when he woke up, he saw the message that their job was well done. However, his master was there cleaning his body, so he could only smile and wait for her to leave.

After spending a little more time with him, she indeed left for Unity’s duel while he waited for Ingrid to come back so they could go together. He needed an excuse to get in, and Ingrid was the best person to take him.

He could have gone with his master, but he first wanted to check the messages of the quests he had completed through his Night Riders and become 15% friends with the Spear Saintess... by being beaten up.

Initially, he expected the quest to end only when he delivered Turyn, who is now sitting powerless in his tower prison, to Alina. However, it seems the tower has evaluated that the quest is completed now that Turyn is in his hands.
⟪ Congratulations! You have completed the first quest in your Chain Quest. You have received your rewards. ⟫
⟪ Rewards: Received ⟫
→ 300,000 Tower Points
→ A Soul Technique (For Elsa)
→ A One Time Summoning Talisman
The points were added, giving him additional money he could spend inside the tower. He did not need to buy things using spirit stones when he could use tower points.
Of course, he wasn’t about to downplay spirit stones just yet. He still needed them in the human world.
He retrieved the Soul Technique, which he had earned for Elsa. She is currently inside the Soul Pagoda in the Soul Gate, learning soul skills as per the requirements her master gave her.
Of course, she is much more attuned to the soul, so while it will take her some time to learn a skill from within the Pagoda, she would, without a doubt, need only a couple of days to do that.
"Soul Piercing Art."

Kent read the technique’s name in his hands, wondering what it was made up of. Of course, he could learn and master it within minutes, but he wasn’t about to take something that belonged to his woman.
"Gaia, make a copy."
He could only copy it and let her learn it first before he would do so. It was always good to have some skills at your fingertips. You never know when you might need them.
⟪ A One Time Summoning Talisman ⟫
→ By channelling your energy into this talisman, you can summon a random being to come to aid you in battle.

→ The being summoned will be based on your luck, so while it can summon an avatar of a god, it can also summon cannon fodder, which in some cases wouldn’t even qualify to be fodder, considering fodders are useful sometimes.
→ The summon will spend 24 hours helping you before they are summoned back to their dimensions and worlds.
→ If the summon wants to stay after 24 hours, you must form a soul contract with them. This contract will be made known when the summon decides to stay.
→ If the summon dies before 24 hours, they will return to their own world and dimensions.
→ You can only use the talisman ones.
"It can be useful or a waste of time at the same time. In fact, it might even be one of those things you receive without any commercial value," Kent said, shaking his head.
He didn’t know why, but after his first summoning ritual, where he got Akira instead of a powerful fighter, he didn’t feel optimistic about this.
’Then again, Akira is overpowered in her own way. I guess getting soul crystals is the best way to utilize her expertise,’ Kent thought before checking the next quest message...
⟪ Congratulations on completing the Quest: Overdue Revenge. You have received your rewards ⟫
⟪ Rewards: Received ⟫
→ 1 Million Tower Points
→ Random Gift Bingo Ticket

Again, he had received loads of tower points for doing nothing. Not that he was about to complain. He is the master of the Night Riders, so their hustle is his hustle. It was only natural to reap the benefits.
’I guess I will let them watch the auction from the tower and let me know if they need anything so I can buy it for them,’ Kent thought inwardly before quickly shifting to the second reward.
He retrieved a card from the tower storage. He had used something similar before, so he knew what had to be done next.
He channelled his spiritual energy into the card, which glowed and vanished as expected. The next second, a message appeared before his vision...
⟪ You have Receive a Gift: Memory Key ⟫
Kent blinked a couple of times when he saw the message. For a minute, he thought Gaia was playing a prank on him, but after blinking some more, he concluded he wasn’t hallucinating.
"What the... f—"
He looked at the message with mixed emotions.
He knew what the key was for... He knew what he saw in the video captured by the tower was true... He knew if he used the key, he would be unlocking a random memory of his past lives.
This meant he would know what kind of person he was or had been in his past lives, and as such, he would know whether he was someone worthy of respect or if he just got lucky.
’The fuck am I thinking... I literally saw over three personalities, and they are all badass.’ Kent grinned, not knowing how to feel at the moment.
Meanwhile, inside the tower, Gaia and Akira stared at each other with a smile playing on their lips.
"I call dibs on the Dragon King," Akira said, holding up a finger.
"You will be wrong. The Dragon King was Master’s first incarnation, but also the one that didn’t count. This means he wouldn’t be awakening that just yet.

He will need to go through a couple of incarnations first, and he has lived quite a few lives. So while he may now possess the first bloodline, I think he will be awakening the Sword Savage (Lord Genesis)."
"How are you sure?" Akira asked, looking as though Gaia had conspired against her.
"Mind Weaver told me many years ago when I asked how incarnations are determined. You know how she is—always calculating improbable outcomes," Gaia smirked.
"That doesn’t change anything. Mind Weaver can be wrong sometimes," Akira said, convinced the Chaos Dragon was about to awaken.ree
"Yes... Mind Weaver can be wrong. But she was only wrong once, and that was when she couldn’t calculate the master’s decision on ultimate sacrifices during the Primordial Wars.
Aside from that, she has never been wrong before, and I doubt she will be this time, too," Gaia said, teasing Akira, who knew she was conspiring against her.
"Fuck..." Akira clenched her tiny fist and said nothing more. She went back to staring at Kent, who held the key, thinking about what to do next.
However, before he could make a decision, Ingrid called out from behind, signalling she was back from her class. Kent put away the key for later.
He would be entering seclusion for now, anyway...

sentences.text: A few hours before the kidnapping game, Kent had passed out after he got his ass handed to him by the Spear Saintess.

Though he wasn’t calling it a beating and more like a duel where he lost, in the end, he passed out and had to spend 10 hours in dreamland, knowing nothing of the mischief his two-night riders were up to.
But when he woke up, he saw the message that their job was well done.
However, his master was there cleaning his body, so he could only smile and wait for her to leave.
After spending a little more time with him, she indeed left for Unity’s duel while he waited for Ingrid to come back so they could go together.
He needed an excuse to get in, and Ingrid was the best person to take him.

He could have gone with his master, but he first wanted to check the messages of the quests he had completed through his Night Riders and become 15% friends with the Spear Saintess... by being beaten up.
Initially, he expected the quest to end only when he delivered Turyn, who is now sitting powerless in his tower prison, to Alina.
However, it seems the tower has evaluated that the quest is completed now that Turyn is in his hands.
⟪ Congratulations!
You have completed the first quest in your Chain Quest.
You have received your rewards. ⟫
⟪ Rewards: Received ⟫
→ 300,000 Tower Points
→ A Soul Technique (For Elsa)
→ A One Time Summoning Talisman
The points were added, giving him additional money he could spend inside the tower.
He did not need to buy things using spirit stones when he could use tower points.
Of course, he wasn’t about to downplay spirit stones just yet.
He still needed them in the human world.
He retrieved the Soul Technique, which he had earned for Elsa.
She is currently inside the Soul Pagoda in the Soul Gate, learning soul skills as per the requirements her master gave her.
Of course, she is much more attuned to the soul, so while it will take her some time to learn a skill from within the Pagoda, she would, without a doubt, need only a couple of days to do that.
"Soul Piercing Art."
Kent read the technique’s name in his hands, wondering what it was made up of.
Of course, he could learn and master it within minutes, but he wasn’t about to take something that belonged to his woman.
"Gaia, make a copy."
He could only copy it and let her learn it first before he would do so.
It was always good to have some skills at your fingertips.
You never know when you might need them.
⟪ A One Time Summoning Talisman ⟫
→ By channelling your energy into this talisman, you can summon a random being to come to aid you in battle.

→ The being summoned will be based on your luck, so while it can summon an avatar of a god, it can also summon cannon fodder, which in some cases wouldn’t even qualify to be fodder, considering fodders are useful sometimes.
→ The summon will spend 24 hours helping you before they are summoned back to their dimensions and worlds.
→ If the summon wants to stay after 24 hours, you must form a soul contract with them.
This contract will be made known when the summon decides to stay.
→ If the summon dies before 24 hours, they will return to their own world and dimensions.
→ You can only use the talisman ones.
"It can be useful or a waste of time at the same time.
In fact, it might even be one of those things you receive without any commercial value," Kent said, shaking his head.
He didn’t know why, but after his first summoning ritual, where he got Akira instead of a powerful fighter, he didn’t feel optimistic about this.
’Then again, Akira is overpowered in her own way.
I guess getting soul crystals is the best way to utilize her expertise,’ Kent thought before checking the next quest message...
⟪ Congratulations on completing the Quest: Overdue Revenge.
You have received your rewards ⟫
⟪ Rewards: Received ⟫
→ 1 Million Tower Points
→ Random Gift Bingo Ticket
Again, he had received loads of tower points for doing nothing.
Not that he was about to complain.
He is the master of the Night Riders, so their hustle is his hustle.
It was only natural to reap the benefits.
’I guess I will let them watch the auction from the tower and let me know if they need anything so I can buy it for them,’ Kent thought inwardly before quickly shifting to the second reward.
He retrieved a card from the tower storage.
He had used something similar before, so he knew what had to be done next.
He channelled his spiritual energy into the card, which glowed and vanished as expected.
The next second, a message appeared before his vision...
⟪ You have Receive a Gift: Memory Key ⟫
Kent blinked a couple of times when he saw the message.
For a minute, he thought Gaia was playing a prank on him, but after blinking some more, he concluded he wasn’t hallucinating.
"What the... f—"
He looked at the message with mixed emotions.
He knew what the key was for...
He knew what he saw in the video captured by the tower was true...
He knew if he used the key, he would be unlocking a random memory of his past lives.
This meant he would know what kind of person he was or had been in his past lives, and as such, he would know whether he was someone worthy of respect or if he just got lucky.
’The fuck am I thinking...
I literally saw over three personalities, and they are all badass.’ Kent grinned, not knowing how to feel at the moment.
Meanwhile, inside the tower, Gaia and Akira stared at each other with a smile playing on their lips.
"I call dibs on the Dragon King," Akira said, holding up a finger.
"You will be wrong.
The Dragon King was Master’s first incarnation, but also the one that didn’t count.
This means he wouldn’t be awakening that just yet.
He will need to go through a couple of incarnations first, and he has lived quite a few lives.
So while he may now possess the first bloodline, I think he will be awakening the Sword Savage (Lord Genesis)."
"How are you sure?" Akira asked, looking as though Gaia had conspired against her.
"Mind Weaver told me many years ago when I asked how incarnations are determined.
You know how she is—always calculating improbable outcomes," Gaia smirked.
"That doesn’t change anything.
Mind Weaver can be wrong sometimes," Akira said, convinced the Chaos Dragon was about to awaken.ree
"Yes...
Mind Weaver can be wrong.
But she was only wrong once, and that was when she couldn’t calculate the master’s decision on ultimate sacrifices during the Primordial Wars.
Aside from that, she has never been wrong before, and I doubt she will be this time, too," Gaia said, teasing Akira, who knew she was conspiring against her.
"Fuck..." Akira clenched her tiny fist and said nothing more.
She went back to staring at Kent, who held the key, thinking about what to do next.
However, before he could make a decision, Ingrid called out from behind, signalling she was back from her class.
Kent put away the key for later.
He would be entering seclusion for now, anyway...

chapters.title: Chapter 206: Going to the Archer Gate
paragraphs: "How was the lecture?" Kent said to Ingrid the moment she stepped out.
"It was informative," Ingrid smiled. ’Theory of Spear Qi’... If she were on Earth, she would have said something like, "I have 3 credit hours on Theory of Spear Qi."

It was one of her favourite lectures, and she never missed it. The instructor was a veteran who had fought in hundreds of battles and encountered hundreds of different experts, so he knew what he was talking about and how best to help a disciple.
Ingrid, who was a nerd in everything, wasn’t about to miss such a lesson. She wanted to understand the fundamentals of Spear Qi and how best to use it in its basic form.
She wanted to study Spear Qi and master it in all aspects. The path she wanted to walk was one of the spears, but her strong suit would be in Spear Qi.
’She wanted to major in Spear Qi... lol.’
"I see. Then, can you escort me to the Archer Gate? I heard there’s a duel between a new genius and an old genius," Kent said, standing up.
"Sure... I was actually here to tell you about the same duel... Looks like someone beat me to it," Ingrid replied.
"Then let’s go. My master is already there... I was just waiting for you." The two left the Spear Gate shortly after, heading toward the Archer Gate.
Of course, the gazes on them were still there as they passed through the Spear Gate, but the two didn’t mind them and just headed toward the Archer Gate.
It took them close to two hours to walk to the colossal gate of the Archer Gate. The moment they appeared at the gate, they were stopped by two guards.
"What business do you have at the Archer Gate?" one of the guards asked arrogantly.
Kent stepped forward, his expression calm but firm. "We’re here to witness the duel between the new genius and the old genius. We’re from the Spear Gate."
The guard narrowed his eyes, looking them up and down.
"Do you have an invitation or proof of permission to enter? The Archer Gate doesn’t allow just anyone to wander in, especially during an event like this."
Ingrid reached into her space ring and pulled out a small token, its surface engraved with intricate symbols. "Here," she said, handing it to the guard. "This should suffice."
The guard took the token, examining it closely. His demeanour shifted slightly, the arrogance fading as he recognized the insignia.
"Ah, I see. My apologies for the inconvenience. You may proceed." He stepped aside, gesturing for them to enter.
As they walked through the gate, Kent glanced at Ingrid. "What was that token? I’ve never seen it before."
Ingrid smirked. "It’s a merit badge given to those who completed a Calamity mission. I earned it about a month ago."
"I see. Then I guess I should hurry up and become a core disciple so I can get one and roam around the sect," Kent said, making Ingrid look at her with an unbelievable expression.
"What?" Kent asked.
"You do know many chase after merit badges so they can join the sect competitions and hopefully make it to the Kingdom Genius competition, right?" Ingrid asked.
Kent just smiled. "My bad... I guess I still have a lot of things to learn. Luckily for me, I have you around to teach and show me the ropes."
Ingrid nodded and puffed out her chest. "I guess I need to teach you a few things before you get into too much trouble... In this sect, it’s not everyone you can provoke."
"Then I will be under your care, Big Sister Ingrid," Kent said, making Ingrid falter in her steps. But she composed herself and kept walking.
Kent just smiled and continued walking toward the centre of the Archer Gate, where the giant arena meant for duels was buzzing with activity.
Just a couple of days ago, a disciple joined the Archer Gate, and within the span of a few days, she has already broken a couple of records.

Records set by some of the best archers in the sect have been shattered by this disciple, who has even set her own. This event immediately captured everyone’s attention. Despite Kent’s wave spreading all over the sect...
Inside the Archer Gate, Unity, who has started making a name for herself, began capturing everyone’s attention. Naturally, the jealous and envious ones came forward.

However, most backed away when they saw her train, and some even retreated when the Gate Master took an interest in her. The Gate Master even took her to a certain training range that measures speed and accuracy.
The training ground has 23 levels, each with its own set of challenges.
Before Unity, the only inner disciple who managed to make a huge stride is now a core disciple and a member of the 27 who will be representing the sect in three months.
But even so, he could only reach the 14th level before he was defeated.

Unity, however, reached the 18th level, four levels higher than the top genius to have ever joined the Archer Gate. This meant Unity has become the kind of disciple that appears only once every 10,000 years.
Naturally, the current top archer in the inner section of the Archer Gate, who only managed to reach the 12th level, wasn’t happy that someone had overshadowed him.
So he challenged her to a duel, and as per the rules of the sect, she had to accept, which was what everyone was excited about.
The old and new geniuses are about to clash in a duel that will show who is who with the bow. Of course, many do not count on Unity, considering she has no battle experience.
But some also want to see some changes, with most sucking up to Unity since she is sisters with a Saintess.
Her popularity is coming from many directions, and if she manages to become the top ranker of the Archer Gate, she will undoubtedly become the next face of the Archer Gate.ree
"Who do you think this new genius is?" Ingrid asked as they neared the arena.
"Probably a blonde-haired beauty with willow eyes and a good handle on her bow," Kent said, making Ingrid look at him weirdly but not say anything.
Kent just smirked, knowing she would hang her jaw when she found out Unity was, in fact, his girlfriend. But for now, they continued to walk until they arrived at the entrance of the giant arena.
There were hundreds of people currently entering, with a few coming and going. Ingrid didn’t join the line; instead, she led Kent to a section where only three people were currently passing through.
Kent didn’t need magic to know they were core disciples, with two even from the Sword Gate. They were wearing different uniforms, just as Ingrid was wearing hers.
Of course, when the two passed, he saw one of them sneakily say something to the elder checking the merit badges. He instinctively knew what was coming but acted like he didn’t see anything.
Instead, he talked to Gaia, and with a smile on his lips, he and Ingrid walked toward the elder, who raised a hand to stop them.
Ingrid retrieved her badge and showed it to the elder. He stepped out of the way and gestured forward. Ingrid walked past him, but he blocked him when Kent was about to pass.
"Only those with merit badges can pass... If you don’t have one but want to enter, you can join the normal queue." The elder said...arrogantly

chapters.title: Chapter 207: Golden Ambrosia Apple
paragraphs: "Is that the troublemaker you were talking about?" A bald man with yellow eyes and a slender figure asked, standing atop a tall building. Beside him were Gate Master Mara and Camilla.
They were staring at Kent, who was approaching the Archer Gate with Ingrid.
"Indeed, he is the disciple of the Sword Saintess," Gate Master Mara answered, looking at Kent with an unreadable expression. At first, she had looked at him with anger in her eyes, but not anymore.
"And you’re saying I should let him pass, else he will create a ruckus?" the old man asked. Gate Master Camilla and Mara nodded.

"If you want your event to go as planned, then be sure to let him pass. You can take it as us owing you a favor each," Gate Master Mara said. After conversing with the sect master, they had come to the Archer Gate to do as they were told.

They had come to peacefully ask the Gate Master of the Archer Gate to cut him some slack. Of course, they knew it wouldn’t be that simple, but they had to try. And, well, it’s safe to say it wasn’t going well.
From what they were seeing in Gate Master Ezra’s eyes, he wanted Kent to cause trouble so he could base his actions on it and take some drastic measures.
Kent’s legend so far had made them uneasy.
One more genius from either gate that wasn’t theirs was a threat to their disciples having a chance to be among the seven to represent the Athea Kingdom in the kingdoms Genius competition.
They could only sigh and watch as Kent and Ingrid entered and walked toward the elder, who was checking the merit badges.
Of course, they saw the core disciple from the Sword Gate, who had told the elder to cause trouble for Kent. Gate Master Mara knew the bastard and planned to handle him after the events.
Since that was the case, they could only pray and hope Kent would play it cool.
So they watched as the elder allowed Ingrid in and then blocked Kent’s path. Using a tone that everyone could hear, he said the magic words:
"Only those with merit badges can pass... If you don’t have one but want to enter, you can join the normal queue."
Kent paused and raised his head, looking at the Elder, who was rather tall for someone his age. Kent had risen to 6’4" when he awakened his bloodline, but the bastard Elder was much taller.

[This is the time you use the catchphrase, Master.] Gaia giggled after saying that. Kent had already made up his mind, so he decided to use the catchphrase like any spoiled brat from a rich background.
"Do you know who I am?" Kent asked, staring at the Elder in the eyes.

"I don’t care who you are. Only those with merit badges can enter here. If you want to enter and don’t have a merit badge, join that queue," the Elder said, pointing at the normal queue with hundreds trying to enter.

"Of course, you can also scram from my sight if you think I will offer you a privilege," the Elder added. The Core disciple from the sword gate, now standing a couple of meters away, smirked at Kent, having offered the Elder a generous reward.
"Allow him, Elder. He is with me," Ingrid tried, but the Elder didn’t budge. She was disappointed, but her reach was limited since this wasn’t the Spear Gate.
"How disappointing," Kent said, shaking his head. He took out a golden apple, bit into it, and began chewing.
It looked juicy, and from how everyone began staring at him with widened eyes, it seemed they wanted some.
Too bad Kent wasn’t in the sharing mood...for he knew what he was doing, and it took just 3 seconds for the result to start showing.
"That is a Golden Ambrosia Apple!" someone in the crowd gasped, their voice trembling with disbelief.
The moment the words left their lips, the atmosphere shifted. Eyes widened, jaws dropped, and murmurs rippled through the crowd like wildfire.
"A Golden Ambrosia Apple? Impossible! The cannot be the golden Ambrosia Apple...No I don’t believe it." A disciple said, looking at the apple Kent was eating with widened eyes.
"Look at the glow! The way it shimmers—it’s real! How does he even have something like that?"
"Those are worth a fortune! No, not just a fortune—they’re priceless! Only the most powerful families or ancient sects could possibly possess one!"
"This is not real, right? This is clearly a dream."
"Yes... This is a dream you will never be able to achieve. Look at the glow. It clearly is a golden Ambrosia apple."
In truth, they are right... The apple Kent is eating is the golden Ambrosia apple, a spirit fruit that, when eaten, enhances one’s cultivation talent to some degree.
Of course, one might wonder why something that affects someone only to a degree is useful. Shouldn’t it be treated like other ordinary fruits? Very ridiculous.
However, that wasn’t why people were drooling over it. The Golden Ambrosia apple has a secondary effect: it upgrades the spirit root of anyone who consumes it by two grades.
Green, Golden, Dark Golden, Jade Diamond, and Celestial White Ambrosia Apples. Those are the categories they come in.
The Green raises the spirit root by 1 grade, Golden by 2, Dark Golden by 3, Jade Diamond by 4, and Celestial White by 5.
Of course, alchemy can help upgrade it too, but with this fruit, once every 100 years, if eaten, it can raise one’s talent and spirit root grade.
The catch is that if the Golden is consumed today, even after 100 years, it wouldn’t have any effect when consumed again. You would have to consume the Dark Golden or higher.
But that is beside the point...

The last time a Golden Ambrosia apple appeared was 57 years ago in the annual auction, and the bidding war lasted for 13 straight hours before the sect master of The Lotus Bloom Valkyrie Sect won it by bidding a whopping 4.3 billion spirit stones.
And here is Kent, chewing on one so casually that everyone was drooling... everyone, including Ingrid, the elder, the bastard core disciple, the normal disciples, and even the three Gate masters.
Everyone wanted it...but nobody wanted to make any sudden moves. Nobody wants to anger Kent, who is the center of attention at the moment...
And then it happened... Kent took out another apple and threw it at Ingrid.

However, that wasn’t why people were drooling over it.
The Golden Ambrosia apple has a secondary effect: it upgrades the spirit root of anyone who consumes it by two grades.
Green, Golden, Dark Golden, Jade Diamond, and Celestial White Ambrosia Apples.
Those are the categories they come in.
The Green raises the spirit root by 1 grade, Golden by 2, Dark Golden by 3, Jade Diamond by 4, and Celestial White by 5.
Of course, alchemy can help upgrade it too, but with this fruit, once every 100 years, if eaten, it can raise one’s talent and spirit root grade.
The catch is that if the Golden is consumed today, even after 100 years, it wouldn’t have any effect when consumed again.
You would have to consume the Dark Golden or higher.
But that is beside the point...

The last time a Golden Ambrosia apple appeared was 57 years ago in the annual auction, and the bidding war lasted for 13 straight hours before the sect master of The Lotus Bloom Valkyrie Sect won it by bidding a whopping 4.3 billion spirit stones.
And here is Kent, chewing on one so casually that everyone was drooling... everyone, including Ingrid, the elder, the bastard core disciple, the normal disciples, and even the three Gate masters.
Everyone wanted it...but nobody wanted to make any sudden moves.
Nobody wants to anger Kent, who is the center of attention at the moment...
And then it happened...
Kent took out another apple and threw it at Ingrid.

chapters.title: Chapter 208: Generous Young Master Kent
paragraphs: Kent threw the Golden Ambrosia Apple, and everyone’s eyes widened.
Ingrid, who was the recipient, quickly recomposed herself and caught the apple with a shocked expression. She couldn’t believe what was happening.

"I wanted to give this and these two Heaven-grade Archer skills to the duel’s winner, but you can have that since they aren’t allowing me to enter. I guess I’ll just burn these two," Kent said, then took another bite of his apple.
"You can tell my master I won’t be joining her since I wasn’t allowed inside," Kent added.

He didn’t need to be a genius to know the normal queue he was asked to join wouldn’t be allowed to enter, considering that from the moment they started approaching the arena, the same person trying to enter from that queue was never permitted—until his situation.
Kent stored the skill books and turned to leave. However, he had only taken two steps when three powerful presences appeared in front of him.
"Gate Master Mara, fancy meeting you here," Kent said with a slightly raised grin.
"Cut it, brat; you’re coming with us," the Gate Master said, taking his hand. Before he could protest, he was whisked away. Ingrid stared at the spot he was taken from and sighed.
Since the Spear Gate Master was also there, she didn’t panic. Instead, she immediately pocketed the apple when she sensed the hungry gazes on it.
She then left to go look for Kent’s master and report the sudden kidnapping of her one true love and disciple.
Meanwhile, Kent was now standing in a garden somewhere in the Spear Gate with three powerful pairs of eyes locked on him. Their auras were enough to crush his dreams and aspirations.
But Kent just stood there, smiling. He didn’t sense any malicious intent from them... Instead, he could tell they wanted something from him.

"Before any of you ask, I won’t tell you where I got the apples from. If you want to buy them, I can give you a good discount since I am generous. This is a once-in-a-lifetime offer," Kent said, munching on the apple.
It wasn’t affecting him, considering he had a Celestial Grade Spirit Root, the highest grade in the universe. To him, the apples he purchased from Gaia for 10,000 Tower Points each were just a snack.
"Name your price," Gate Master Ezra said.
"Why don’t you give me your offer first? If I like it, I will sell... else, I’ll just keep it to myself," Kent replied. He wouldn’t mind giving it to them for free... he just didn’t want to.
Why...?

That was because he didn’t trust any of them, but he also knew they wouldn’t do anything to him, considering word had already begun spreading about the apples he pulled out. He is of interest at the moment.
He was a hot commodity now; if he wanted, he could just open a shop and start selling.

He had nearly infinite apples to choose from, and it was all thanks to the Lost Garden of Alrighan, currently floating somewhere in the cosmos, housing millions of such apples ranging from Golden to Jade Diamond.
"What do you want?" Gate Master Mara asked. Instead of making an offer, she knew Kent wouldn’t accept money. He was too rich to take money for something like this.
This could only mean he wanted something.
"Glad you asked," Kent said with a smile. "I was just stopped because I don’t have a merit badge. Though it’s a bummer, I also got to know that only core disciples can have one.

Now, I’m not asking you to make me a core disciple. I just want the chance to pick a Calamity mission whenever I want, even as an Inner disciple," Kent said, and Gate Master Mara could only look at him with a weird expression.
Kent didn’t say anything else; he just waited for her answer. She was the only one he knew, despite being aware of the names and identities of the two with her.
"Is that all?" she asked, checking to see if Kent was just messing with her. She had been following him for a few days, so she knew Kent was a brat.
"That’s all. Though I planned to join the sect competition by beating Randy up, I also knew it wouldn’t be that easy. So, do this, and I’ll give you one Golden Ambrosia Apple," Kent replied.
"Done," Gate Master Mara said.
"Then here you go," Kent said, handing over the apple. He turned to the two gate masters.

"You must be the gate master for the Spear Gate. Pleasure meeting you," Kent said with a smile. Gate Master Camilla, who had been bragging that she would turn him into her boy toy, was now at a loss for words.
She was standing close to Kent, and his smile and handsome features seemed to have taken her breath away.
Gate Master Mara, who had what she wanted, scoffed upon seeing this.
"Let’s get down to business then. All I want from you is...*...*" Kent whispered something that made the gate master raise an eyebrow and turn to Gate Master Mara before she nodded.
The sudden conversation made Gate Master Mara raise an eyebrow in suspicion, but they didn’t say anything.
Kent handed her an apple as well. Then he turned to the male gate master of the Archer Gate.
"I just wanted to watch the duel in peace, but it seems your elders aren’t ethical enough. So, while I hate this, I would like it if the elder was dismissed immediately.
That will make up for the embarrassment he put me through," Kent said in a righteous tone, making the two lady gate masters look at him strangely.
Even without the appearance of the apple, the gate master was already going to fire the elder for allowing himself to be influenced by an outside force.
Letting his greed get the best of him was his mistake...
So, to think he was offering something this priceless for something so simple—the Spear Gate Master would be a fool not to take it.

Kent would even kill the sect elder just to appease him if he wanted. The act committed by the sect elder was unethical, so he can be subjected to some serious punishments. However, Kent just wanted him sacked.
Knowing he was indeed not qualified to pass through the easy door was enough for him to ask for a much softer punishment. There is no honour in asking for more than one deserves.
Like he said, he was being generous today because he was happy.
"Done," Gate master Ezra said with conviction.
"Then here you go," Kent said, handing the apple to him.
"Now, if you don’t mind, I’d like to go watch the duel between geniuses. Who knows, I might take a liking to one of them," Kent said before turning around.
The next second, he was transported away, leaving only the three gate masters in stunned silence. The only question on their minds was: ’Who is this kid?’

chapters.title: Chapter 209: The Old Vs New (1)
paragraphs: Kent used the connection between himself and his master—since she is part of his harem—to teleport inside the arena. He appeared in a room where the Saintess was checking to see if Unity’s armor was perfect.
Of course, it was perfect, but she was just being a supportive sister to her.
"Kent... you’re here," Unity said the moment Kent appeared inside the room.
"Sorry for the lateness. I had some minor setbacks, but I’m here now," Kent said, walking toward her. The Saintess was also done checking her already perfect armor.
"I’m glad that you both are here," Unity said with a sigh. She seemed to finally be at peace.
"You seem on edge," Kent commented. "Don’t tell me you’re having cold feet."
"No, that’s not it. Though I never wanted this duel to happen, I guess I’m just too afraid I might not have good control of my skills and accidentally kill him," Unity said, making Kent smirk.
"This sect is full of cowards, so they made it so you don’t really die even if you die," Kent said, turning to his master. "No offense."

The Saintess just shrugged and placed her hands on Unity’s shoulders. "You don’t have to worry about accidentally killing him. Death is not permanent, so show everyone what you’re made of, as Big Sister Vexthra said."
Unity nodded, leaving Kent to wonder what the ladies had talked about. But since they weren’t sharing, he chose to let it slide for now.
"You ladies should continue; I have some business with the referee," Kent said before walking away.
Fifteen minutes later, everyone was seated and ready for the duel to determine the genius between Unity and Rand.
Kent was already back and seated with his master and Ingrid, who still couldn’t understand how Kent got in.
Of course, Kent lied and said the Gate Master brought him in, but she didn’t believe him—not in the slightest.
This resulted from the shocking discovery that Kent possessed not one but multiple Golden Ambrosia apples; now, she also had one.
In truth, she kept blinking a couple of times to see if she was asleep or if this was actually happening.
Of course, Kent spent no effort telling her or answering any of her many questions. In truth, he only bought the fruit when he saw the core disciple whisper to the elder and look in his direction.
He managed to enter by shutting him up. Of course, Kent wasn’t actually planning on running away. He just wanted to leave so he could enter using the harem teleport ability.
But now that his showing off had gone too far, he could only hope this wouldn’t create too much trouble for him. Ingrid was one of those troubles. She seemed to want answers to every single thing.
Kent could only smile as Unity walked into the arena, holding her soul weapon called [Unity’s Bow]. It was the bow Vexthra made for her.
She also had a quiver on her back, but it only held three arrows.
They were ordinary arrows, but she just wanted to keep them there so that she would look cool and appear like an archer.
Or maybe they held some value...
When she entered, many began cheering for her, especially the boys, who Kent knew were thinking and imagining all kinds of nasty things—just as he was doing at the moment.
Unity might not have the curves like his other ladies, but she was undoubtedly gorgeous. So, no matter what, she was eye candy to many.
The moment she settled into her spot, a young man about Kent’s height, with short dark hair and dark pupils, walked into the arena, exuding a cold, icy aura.
As he walked inside, every step left a frozen footprint, freezing the ground behind him as he moved further into the arena.

Just like with Unity, the cheers for him were even louder. Kent looked at his showing off and gave him an 8 out of 10. Though he wanted his woman to win, he had to admit the guy knew how to show off and make an entrance.
He walked to his spot, maintaining a 300-meter distance between them. This was a duel between archers, and distance was essential, among other things.
Kent looked at this setup and nodded. However, he would be lying if he said he wasn’t worried about his woman.

Among his women, Unity was the mystery. He knew next to nothing about her true potential. Perhaps it was because she had only recently begun walking the path of an archer, but even before that, she had been an enigma.
The tower was able to determine that she possessed a very powerful bloodline. However, it wasn’t able to determine just how powerful she was.
Even after the tower awakened, Gaia still couldn’t determine her potential, unlike how she had with Elsa. So, Kent was somewhat biased toward her.
It was also the reason why he decided to use the True Name Token on her, to see if her true potential was anything close to Elsa’s, who was now the most powerful soul cultivator in the world.
He wanted to see if his woman could finally let go of her past identity as Lilian’s maid and feel comfortable being herself.
She still, in a way, saw herself as Lilian’s maid, so Kent wanted to ensure she realized her dream much faster.
So, while he couldn’t say he wasn’t worried she might lose, he was also rooting for her to win. In the end, it was she who would determine whether she would win or lose.
"Thank you all for coming," the elder acting as the referee said.
"Before we start, I have an announcement to make," the elder continued, taking out a jade box that looked expensive. The moment the box appeared, everyone quieted down.

"This box was delivered to me just now. Per the instructions left, whoever wins this duel will be receiving it. And though the winner can only open it, one of the items within is a Heaven Grade Bow skill."
