chapters.title: Chapter 210: The Old Vs New (2)
paragraphs: The moment the elder said those words, everyone’s expression changed. In fact, even the elders watching looked into each other’s faces, and one could see their greed.
On the ground, Rand tightened his grip on his bow when he heard the words. To him, this was a once-in-a-lifetime chance to acquire a heaven-grade skill since they are very expensive.
On the other hand, Unity maintained her calm expression, but inwardly, she was talking to Kent.
⟪Is this your doing?⟫
[Yes. I wanted to spice things up a bit,] Kent replied while maintaining a calm expression since Ingrid was staring daggers at him with suspicion in her eyes.
⟪But I already have four heaven-grade skills and even a divine-grade cultivation technique; I don’t need any more skills.⟫ Unity said.

[I know. That was why I only left ice bow skills in the box. There are also a couple of some things inside. If you win, you can be generous and gift them to your opponent,] Kent said through telepathy, making Unity sigh.
She doesn’t need the skills, considering she can get one whenever possible. Vexthra has already told them to milk Kent dry. But she also has millions of spirit stones, thanks to Kent’s generosity.
So, while Heaven grade skills might be the most amazing thing for people like Rand, she didn’t lack any. She could even get one if she talked to her sister, who is a goddess.
Having someone like Vexthra sure has its perks.
Even Kent would want to brag about that, mainly because Vexthra has proven her worth many times, so while she cannot come down and help him, she can do it in her own way.
⟪Then, thank you in advance,⟫ Unity said before focusing back on her opponent.
"You already know the rules. Go all out, and don’t worry about dying... only worry about the pain of dying."
Unity and Rand nodded and focused on each other.
"Begin."
The moment the elder gave the order, Unity and Rand took action. A powerful ice qi burst out of Rand’s body, filling the space with its icy coldness.
He brandished his bow, and a long, thick arrow formed from frost appeared in his bow.
Pulling the bowstring, a chilling ice exuded from the bow, and then he let loose the string, sending out an arrow and a trail of frost in its wake.
On the other hand, Unity also brandished her bow and took out one of the arrows in her quiver, locking it in her bow.
It was a simple arrow, but the moment she released the bowstring, a powerful force shot the arrow forward.
The two arrows raced toward each other, cutting through the air with precision.
Rand’s frost arrow left a trail of icy mist, freezing the ground beneath it, while Unity’s arrow, though seemingly ordinary, carried an overwhelming force that distorted the air around it.

The arrows collided midair with a deafening crack. Rand’s frost arrow shattered into countless icy shards, scattering like glittering dust, while Unity’s arrow continued its trajectory, barely slowed.
Rand’s eyes widened in shock as he swiftly dodged to the side, the arrow grazing his arm and leaving a shallow cut.
The shocked him
It wasn’t just him who was shocked. Even Unity herself was stunned by the unexpected power of that shot.
She had only intended to test one of the skills Vexthra had embedded in the bow—a skill called [Unbreaking Arrow].

The skill allowed Unity to imbue her arrows with spiritual energy, and while she was only a Root Grandmaster, the skill multiplied the amount of energy she infused by five. That was all there was to it.
What she never anticipated was that her arrow would be so devastatingly powerful. It became clear to her that her foundation rebuilding had been far more successful than she had realized.
If such a small amount of her energy could produce such a result, what would happen if she poured more energy into it?
Strangely, despite taking an arrow from her quiver, three still remain, meaning that somehow, the arrow she fired has returned to the quiver or was replaced.
All the same, she only had three in the quiver and shot one, yet three still remained.
But that can wait until the duel is over to investigate.
Rand was shocked that he nearly lost his arm in the first exchange, which would have been disastrous for him, considering losing a duel after a single exchange would have been too disgraceful.
Rand nocked another frost arrow without hesitation, this time infusing it with even more qi. The air around him grew colder, and frost crept up his arms.
He released the arrow, which split into three mid-flight, each one homing in on Unity from different angles.
Unity remained calm, her expression unreadable.
She quickly drew the three arrows from her quiver, firing them in rapid succession. Each of her arrows intercepted one of Rand’s frost arrows, causing them to explode into bursts of icy mist.
The crowd watching gasped at the display of skill and precision.
[Though you are a monster master, I think Unity is someone meant to wield the bow. Her precision and speed are admirable.]
Gaia’s voice echoed in Kent’s mind, bringing a smile to his face.
Indeed, Unity’s display was impeccable. It was just like how Kent was with the sword. Her control, and even her demeanor as arrows sped toward her, showed she was in the moment—one with her bow.
She wasn’t behaving like Rand, who seemed to be panicking at the display. He was firing icy arrows, but Unity was countering every one of them.
Kent couldn’t help but watch the duel with a smile. Though one might wonder how two archers could duel, seeing it now changed everything.
Watching as pointed arrows met midair and exploded, or sometimes one cutting through the other... one couldn’t help but admire it.
They weren’t using any active skills yet, but Rand wasn’t having it easy.
He fired an arrow that was twice as fast and deadlier than the previous ones, but Unity countered it with her own arrow, shattering the thick ice arrow effortlessly.
Rand gritted his teeth, realizing he was being outmatched. He changed tactics, channeling his qi into the ground beneath him.
A wave of ice surged forward, spreading rapidly toward Unity in an attempt to trap her in a frozen prison.
Unity, however, was already a step ahead. She leaped into the air, her movements graceful and fluid, evading the icy wave.

While midair, she drew another arrow, this time infusing it with a faint golden glow. She released it, and the arrow streaked toward Rand like a light beam, forcing him to dive to the ground to avoid it.
The arrow struck the ground behind him, creating a small crater and sending a shockwave through the arena.
Rand got up and realized he had to act fast; otherwise, he would lose.
He extended his fingers and pulled on the bowstring. This time, a green arrow made of ice materialized in the bow, and instantly, the surroundings were plunged into an icy coldness.
"Penetrating Ice Killing Arrow!"
He shouted as ice qi surged from his body and bow. Then he released it, and the entire space between Unity and him froze as the arrow sped toward her.

sentences.text: The moment the elder said those words, everyone’s expression changed.
In fact, even the elders watching looked into each other’s faces, and one could see their greed.
On the ground, Rand tightened his grip on his bow when he heard the words.
To him, this was a once-in-a-lifetime chance to acquire a heaven-grade skill since they are very expensive.
On the other hand, Unity maintained her calm expression, but inwardly, she was talking to Kent.
⟪Is this your doing?⟫
[Yes.
I wanted to spice things up a bit,] Kent replied while maintaining a calm expression since Ingrid was staring daggers at him with suspicion in her eyes.
⟪But I already have four heaven-grade skills and even a divine-grade cultivation technique; I don’t need any more skills.⟫ Unity said.
[I know.
That was why I only left ice bow skills in the box.
There are also a couple of some things inside.
If you win, you can be generous and gift them to your opponent,] Kent said through telepathy, making Unity sigh.
She doesn’t need the skills, considering she can get one whenever possible.
Vexthra has already told them to milk Kent dry.
But she also has millions of spirit stones, thanks to Kent’s generosity.
So, while Heaven grade skills might be the most amazing thing for people like Rand, she didn’t lack any.
She could even get one if she talked to her sister, who is a goddess.
Having someone like Vexthra sure has its perks.
Even Kent would want to brag about that, mainly because Vexthra has proven her worth many times, so while she cannot come down and help him, she can do it in her own way.
⟪Then, thank you in advance,⟫ Unity said before focusing back on her opponent.
"You already know the rules.
Go all out, and don’t worry about dying... only worry about the pain of dying."
Unity and Rand nodded and focused on each other.
"Begin."
The moment the elder gave the order, Unity and Rand took action.
A powerful ice qi burst out of Rand’s body, filling the space with its icy coldness.
He brandished his bow, and a long, thick arrow formed from frost appeared in his bow.
Pulling the bowstring, a chilling ice exuded from the bow, and then he let loose the string, sending out an arrow and a trail of frost in its wake.
On the other hand, Unity also brandished her bow and took out one of the arrows in her quiver, locking it in her bow.
It was a simple arrow, but the moment she released the bowstring, a powerful force shot the arrow forward.
The two arrows raced toward each other, cutting through the air with precision.
Rand’s frost arrow left a trail of icy mist, freezing the ground beneath it, while Unity’s arrow, though seemingly ordinary, carried an overwhelming force that distorted the air around it.
The arrows collided midair with a deafening crack.
Rand’s frost arrow shattered into countless icy shards, scattering like glittering dust, while Unity’s arrow continued its trajectory, barely slowed.
Rand’s eyes widened in shock as he swiftly dodged to the side, the arrow grazing his arm and leaving a shallow cut.
The shocked him
It wasn’t just him who was shocked.
Even Unity herself was stunned by the unexpected power of that shot.
She had only intended to test one of the skills Vexthra had embedded in the bow—a skill called [Unbreaking Arrow].
The skill allowed Unity to imbue her arrows with spiritual energy, and while she was only a Root Grandmaster, the skill multiplied the amount of energy she infused by five.
That was all there was to it.
What she never anticipated was that her arrow would be so devastatingly powerful.
It became clear to her that her foundation rebuilding had been far more successful than she had realized.
If such a small amount of her energy could produce such a result, what would happen if she poured more energy into it?
Strangely, despite taking an arrow from her quiver, three still remain, meaning that somehow, the arrow she fired has returned to the quiver or was replaced.
All the same, she only had three in the quiver and shot one, yet three still remained.
But that can wait until the duel is over to investigate.
Rand was shocked that he nearly lost his arm in the first exchange, which would have been disastrous for him, considering losing a duel after a single exchange would have been too disgraceful.
Rand nocked another frost arrow without hesitation, this time infusing it with even more qi.
The air around him grew colder, and frost crept up his arms.
He released the arrow, which split into three mid-flight, each one homing in on Unity from different angles.
Unity remained calm, her expression unreadable.
She quickly drew the three arrows from her quiver, firing them in rapid succession.
Each of her arrows intercepted one of Rand’s frost arrows, causing them to explode into bursts of icy mist.
The crowd watching gasped at the display of skill and precision.
[Though you are a monster master, I think Unity is someone meant to wield the bow.
Her precision and speed are admirable.]
Gaia’s voice echoed in Kent’s mind, bringing a smile to his face.
Indeed, Unity’s display was impeccable.
It was just like how Kent was with the sword.
Her control, and even her demeanor as arrows sped toward her, showed she was in the moment—one with her bow.
She wasn’t behaving like Rand, who seemed to be panicking at the display.
He was firing icy arrows, but Unity was countering every one of them.
Kent couldn’t help but watch the duel with a smile.
Though one might wonder how two archers could duel, seeing it now changed everything.
Watching as pointed arrows met midair and exploded, or sometimes one cutting through the other... one couldn’t help but admire it.
They weren’t using any active skills yet, but Rand wasn’t having it easy.
He fired an arrow that was twice as fast and deadlier than the previous ones, but Unity countered it with her own arrow, shattering the thick ice arrow effortlessly.
Rand gritted his teeth, realizing he was being outmatched.
He changed tactics, channeling his qi into the ground beneath him.
A wave of ice surged forward, spreading rapidly toward Unity in an attempt to trap her in a frozen prison.
Unity, however, was already a step ahead.
She leaped into the air, her movements graceful and fluid, evading the icy wave.
While midair, she drew another arrow, this time infusing it with a faint golden glow.
She released it, and the arrow streaked toward Rand like a light beam, forcing him to dive to the ground to avoid it.
The arrow struck the ground behind him, creating a small crater and sending a shockwave through the arena.

chapters.title: Chapter 211: The Old Vs New (3)
paragraphs: The arrow was one of Rand’s trump cards.
Penetrating Ice Killing Arrow.
He learned this skill from the Bow Tower when he became an Inner Disciple three years ago. In fact, if one were to ask him, he would say that skill was one of his strongest skills.
The skill taps into his core ice and forms an arrow from it.
This core ice is the strongest form of his ice element, and the arrow is formed from it. While he wouldn’t say it was easy, he also never expected Unity to survive that.
An arrow formed from the core ice is something nobody can easily defend against, especially someone as weak as Unity, who wasn’t even a Root Saint yet.
Just like Kent, she was also at the Level 8 Root Grandmaster stage. But when the arrow came speeding toward her, she remained calm and retrieved a single arrow from her quiver.
She nocked it into her bow and imbued it with her energy. She was still not using her lightning element, so it was a pure brute attack.
She released the arrow, and as expected, the two met 70 meters from Unity.
This time, instead of both arrows exploding immediately, the two met and remained still for five seconds before a powerful explosion of ice rocked the arena.
The explosion sent a shockwave rippling through the arena, shattering the ground and sending shards of ice flying in all directions.
The crowd gasped, their breaths visible in the sudden chill that enveloped the battlefield.
Rand stood firm, his bow still raised, his eyes narrowed as he searched through the icy haze for any sign of Unity.
He couldn’t believe she had managed to counter his core ice arrow, even if only partially.
But then, a faint glow emerged through the swirling mist of frost and debris.
Unity stepped forward, her bow held steady, her expression calm but her eyes blazing with determination.
The explosion sent out more shockwaves than she anticipated, but she managed to regain her footing and was now back for more.
Rand’s jaw tightened.

He clenched his fist, drew his bow, and leaped into the air. At the same time, a powerful energy burst out of his body, making everyone watching, especially the inner disciples, realize Rand wished to end the battle.
This was his classic move.
"Wailing of the Ice," he muttered as he pulled on his bowstring.
He pulled back with much greater force, but if one looked closely, they wouldn’t see any arrow in his bow.
’Where did the arrow go?’ Unity wondered, but she remained alert.
Suddenly, she pulled on her bow as well.
This was because, just as she was looking toward Rand, a five-layered spell circle appeared in the air to the left of her location.
If Rand were a mage, he would have been regarded as a High Mage for having the energy to form a five-layered spell circle.
But it formed, and from within the spell circle, a thick arrow made of pure green ice appeared. That wasn’t all—around the arrow, five wraiths coiled around it, screeching icy energy.
Unity’s expression changed.
The arrow coming at her was not simple, and from the paleness on Rand’s face, one could tell he had placed all his hopes and dreams in that arrow.
Unity jumped into the air and moved back, creating some distance between herself and the arrow.
She then closed her eyes and pulled on her bowstring.
Everyone watching observed her calmly, wondering what she was up to, closing her eyes mid-battle.
But it didn’t take long for everyone to see she wasn’t making any mistake; instead, she was unlocking something.
In truth, Unity was just conversing with her big sister, who had placed a seal on her lightning element while working on her foundation.
Vexthra had done that to ensure Unity mastered her bow using her own strength and speed. But now that the odds had changed and she might lose, Unity told her to lift the seal.
Vexthra didn’t ask why. She had already expected Unity to ask her to lift the seal days ago, but Unity hadn’t.
So Vexthra lifted the seal, and at once, a powerful golden lightning burst out of Unity’s body, lighting up the air.
Everyone gasped as the lightning spread throughout the arena, threatening to destroy everything. Kent watched this with a smile.

He also possessed a lightning element, golden in hue, but looking at Unity’s, he could tell they were completely different. In fact, he could even feel it—Unity was different the moment the lightning appeared.
An arrow formed in her bow, crafted from thick lightning.
"Judgement Arrow," Unity muttered, and then she snapped her eyes open. "Two Times Exploding."
She released the arrow, and it streaked through the air like lightning, colliding with the ice arrow. The impact exploded into sparkles of ice and lightning.
It was a powerful yet beautiful explosion, but the shockwave only rippled through the air.
Unity was back on the ground, and like lightning, she moved. The next second, she stood before Rand with an arrow pointed at his neck.
He had lost the duel and he knows it.
Unity used one of the skills she had acquired from the green bazaar. Aside from [Heaven’s Arrowstorm] and [Thunder God’s Precision], she had also purchased one called [Judgement Arrow].
Though the name sounded impressive, the skill itself was monstrous.
It allowed Unity to form arrows from her lightning element, and then, using her mastery of the element, she could multiply the explosive power of the arrow.
This time, she was able to multiply it by two. But if her mastery increased, she could multiply it by higher percentages. It all depended on her mastery of lightning.
Rand, who was as pale as paper from the exhaustion he had sustained from using the powerful skill, sighed. He didn’t need anyone to tell him he had indeed lost.

Though he would have liked to think he hadn’t lost, he could also tell a new monster had emerged. He may be a monster, but he still paled compared to Unity, whose talent with the bow was unparalleled.
Of course, she would soon find out how unparallel she really is with the bow. For now, she is just Unity with the bow...

chapters.title: Chapter 212: Generous Unity
paragraphs: "Good fight," Rand said, standing up.
Unity nodded at his words. The fight was indeed a good one, and they enjoyed it very much from the look on everyone’s faces.
A battle between two geniuses was always a spectacle in the sect. So, while some people expected Rand to win, they also had to give it to Unity; she had some skills.
"We should duel some other time," Rand said, accepting his defeat but not losing his will and determination to walk the path of the Bow and Arrow.
"I would love that," Unity chose to be polite.

The elder who acted as the referee entered the arena carrying the jade box. Rand saw this and could only sigh. Though he would love to have his hands on the box’s contents, he also knew today wasn’t his chance.
"Since you are the winner of this duel, this box and its contents go to you," the elder said, handing it over to Unity.
One had to give credit to this ’anonymous’ person. Just the box alone was enough to buy another Heaven-grade treasure. Kent found out that all the packaging Gaia did was free.
So he requested the best item, only to receive a jade box that would sell for millions. He could only thank her and accept her generous package.
Unity took the box and gently pried it open. Everyone quieted down, some straining their eyes to see if they could glimpse the contents inside. But that was a futile effort.
Unity looked at the items in the box and smiled inwardly. Of course, a shocked expression appeared on her face, but she quickly recovered.
She sighed again, took a golden apple from the box, and placed it into her space ring. This action caught the attention of a few people, with only four recognizing the fruit she had stored away.
Ingrid, who recognized this fruit, immediately knew Kent was the anonymous donor. This finally led her to conclude that Kent is indeed the richest person in the world.
Of course, he is the richest—he has the two who can steal...ahem, retrieve anything from the cosmos and beyond as his assistants. Nothing is impossible to him...
Unity closed the box and looked toward Rand.

"Take it... I already have enough skills I haven’t mastered yet, and these ones are even ice-based. They are perfect for you. Also, there’s a little money in there to get you a new bow; spend it well," Unity said, extending the box toward him.
Rand and everyone else’s eyes snapped wide open at the sudden turn of events. Was she really handing over something this expensive to a complete stranger?

But that just didn’t make sense. Heaven-grade skills were the highest one could acquire in this world. A few possessed Legendary-grade skills, and there were even rumors that the Elves, Demons, and Dragons had Mystical-grade skills.
But right now, the strongest one could attain was Heaven-grade.
So why would she just give it away like that? It simply didn’t make sense.
"Are you sure?" Rand asked. Though he wanted the skill books, he also couldn’t understand why she gave them so freely.

"I have no use for them, and since you have ice affinity, I can only give it to you. Don’t worry. If I need something and you can help me in the future, I won’t hesitate to ask," Unity said with a small smile.
She is the wife of this duel’s richest and most generous anonymous donor, so she doesn’t need this stuff. But aside from that, there was also another reason...

Unity was a maid before becoming Kent’s woman, so though Rand may appear arrogant and nonchalant, she could see herself in him. He was someone like her, so while this was perfect, she also didn’t want to turn a blind eye to him.
Kent was watching this with a calm expression.

He had already checked Rand’s profile and knew who he was to a certain extent. This also means that when Saden comes and asks for permission to go after the Malric Noble Family, he would even give her additional support.

Though Rand hadn’t told anyone, he was a twin who lost his sister to the Malric family. They were servants in their household, but due to the sinister schemes of the Malric family, his sister was never seen or heard from again.
He ran and came to the sect. Luckily, his talent and undying will to one day avenge his sister pushed him to train hard.
So, he may have lost, but to him, getting revenge for his sister was more important than today’s defeat.
"Go ahead, take it," Unity said, and finally, Rand took it.
"Thank you," Rand said, wiping a tear from his face.

"Don’t worry about it. I’ll see you around, and when you’re done mastering the skills, we can have another duel, though I doubt you’ll be able to win," Unity smiled and walked away, leaving Rand, who was now the center of attention.
Luckily, the gate master appeared in the arena the next second and led him away. He took him straight to the Bow Tower, where Rand would be safe to learn the skills.
Of course, the gate master was interested in the skills, but he also stuck to his values and let Rand keep what he had earned.
Just like that, the events of the Archer Gate were over.
Rand had gotten two heaven-grade skills, 100 million spirit stones, and a jade box worth millions. It was a good haul for him.
Meanwhile, Unity had become everyone’s favorite.
Her generosity was just too moving. All those who initially wanted her to lose were now her biggest fans, meaning Unity had now become someone very important in the Archer Gate.
This also concluded Kent’s plan to make her feel included.
She may have been Lilian’s maid, but now, she had become her own person.
Unity, the genius of the Archer Gate in the inner section. Even the core disciples who came to witness the duel now saw her in a new light, with a few having lustful thoughts.
Naturally, they would learn it hard if they tried anything funny.
Kent left with Ingrid, who still had many questions. However, Saintess Selene stayed with Unity for a few hours before leaving.

chapters.title: Chapter 213: Her True Gift For Winning [18+]
paragraphs: Unity moaned as she bounced up and down on Kent’s lap.
His dick was buried deep inside her as she rode him like a cowgirl. Kent held her hips, ensuring every movement sent waves of pleasure through both their bodies.

Unity had been in the cowgirl position for the past four hours, and Kent was giving her exactly what she wanted. She rode him passionately, and from the looks on their faces, it was clear they were both thoroughly enjoying it.
This was her true gift for winning the duel, after all.
After Kent left the Archer Gate with Ingrid, he returned to the Spear Gate, where he spent a couple of hours answering her endless stream of questions.
One had to admit, the lady had an abundance of curiosity. She might have been the perfect friend if it weren’t for her persistent nature and refusal to take no for an answer.
But Kent didn’t mind; he indulged her questions and even added more to satisfy her curiosity. After ending their talk, he returned to the sword gate since the Spear Saintess was still not secluded.
When he got back, he waited for his master to return before contacting Unity to meet him in the harem tower, where he planned to give her the actual reward he had prepared for her...
His dick.
Unity, of course, wasn’t about to pass up on this offer, so she freshened up and, using the authority Kent had given to all his women, entered the tower where Kent was waiting for her.
Thus, using the time difference to their advantage, they began their lovemaking, which at the moment saw Unity riding down the old town road.
"Mmmmhh"
"Aaahh"

"Gaia, do you perhaps have a way to keep my women on the outside and at the same time inside the tower? I feel like they should spend more time inside the tower since everything here is just better," Kent asked.
Gaia appeared beside him the next second, wearing a pondering expression.

[I have a skill called [Perfect Cloning]. This skill will allow them to create a perfect clone of themselves that they can either use to stay on the outside while the real body is in the tower or the clone can stay in the tower while the real body remains on the outside.]

[You currently have 9,500,700 tower points from all the duels you fought and won, along with some completed quests. So, do more and earn more, I guess.]
Gaia giggled, but Kent ignored her and focused on his main objective. "Do you still have the tracker on Manager Alina active?"
[Yes. She arrived in Vastport City yesterday and is currently staying in the most secure suite at the Evermore Green Life Hotel.]
"Good. Then, I guess it is time to pay a visit to our friend." Kent smiled and then teleported away, appearing in front of a mountain cave.
If one looked closely, it was similar to the Makosa Prison, the same place where he had rescued Li Hua from when the Ashland noble kidnapped her.
This was Gaia’s doing, considering she had asked permission to design the prison a few weeks ago.
"This reminds me, Gaia, do you have a way to retrieve that thing below the real Makosa Prison?" Kent asked.

[I left some markers then, and from what I found out, the item is some kind of special artifact that requires a great understanding of spatial law. Of course, I can easily retrieve it, but that would be a loss.

This will help you start to become familiar with spatial law, and if you are good enough, you can even begin learning space law.]

Basically, anyone sent there has no hope of coming back out again. Per the rules of the prison, all those sent there will lose their cultivation—or rather, have it locked—rendering them powerless.

He has been in there for weeks now, considering the time difference. He is now akin to a mortal, and his hunger at the moment was boiling over.
He was brought in 19 hours ago, which amounts to 19 days inside the prison. As a mortal, he needed food and water, but he was no ordinary mortal.

paragraphs: Turyn turned toward Kent the moment he heard him speak. Hope in his mind has arrived...It has been days already since he arrived in the Tower Prison...
In fact, for the first few days after he arrived in this place, he had screamed for someone to come to his rescue. But after three days, he realized he was alone.
This prompted him to give up and live the rest of his days listening to and enduring the harrowing sounds produced by the bats.
He never had any hope of being rescued. So when Kent spoke, it was as if an angel had been sent to rescue him.
Well, that was his initial thought—until he saw the smile on Kent’s face, and his body froze. Then, the words Kent spoke echoed in his head, and he knew exactly who the young man in front of him was.
"Who are you... where am I?" Turyn asked, crawling back to the opposite side of the wall. He could tell the person in front of him had a hand in his current predicament.
"The irony, isn’t it?" Kent said, pulling out a chair and sitting down on the opposite side, just outside the metal doors.
Gaia had stolen that concept from prison cells on Earth.

"You used to tie down and imprison young ladies so you could have your way with them. Now, look at you—the dignified, perverted heir of the Miller family, reduced to this. How the mighty have fallen," Kent said, his voice laced with disdain.
"Who are you?" Turyn asked again, this time panicking.
"I am a nobody who happened to not mind my own business, so here we are. But while we are at it, can I know more about you, your work, and your life?" Kent asked.

Turyn didn’t answer as he was panicking and tears began rolling down his face. He was pampered so much that this was his first time experiencing something like this, and it wasn’t a pleasant experience.
"Won’t talk, huh? Not that I expected much. But tell me, do you happen to know a lady by the name of Alina?" Kent asked.
"I don’t know who you are talking about...Please let me go, and I will reward you generously," Turyn said, still crying.
"You don’t know who I am talking about", Kent said, gritting his teeth. "You don’t know who I am talking about" His eyes flashed, and lightning danced across it.
"AAaaaaahgggghh"
A horse cream filled the prison as Kent extended his fingers and short a golden lightning bolt at Turyn, who was now screaming and rolling on the ground.
"Now, I will ask again, and you would have to do well to remember," Kent said, looking coldly at Turyn.
"Now I dare ask, do you know anyone by the name Alina?" Kent asked again, but Turyn didn’t seem to recall who he was talking about.
"Please let me go. I don’t know who you are talking about," He said, but Kent only extended his finger, and a bolt of lightning bombarded the bastard.
"You can either keep quiet and recall the faces and names of all the ladies you have defiled and destroyed all for your canal pleasures. People like you don’t deserve to have easy endings.
So take your time, for you have a lot of those. I will just be here asking every two minutes, and until you manage to give me a good answer, prepare to receive a blast.
And don’t worry, you won’t die from the lightning. That will be mercy, so take your time, for the more time you waste, the more chances I will have to torture you."
Kent leaned back on his chair while he observed Turyn, who was groaning with a few burnt skin here and there. Ken wasn’t making things easy on him.
Two minutes later, another painful groan filled the prison cell. It was two minutes later and he still hadn’t recall who Alina was.
In truth, Kent knew he wouldn’t be able to remember Alina, considering the issue with her that had happened 20 years ago. Alina was just 18 when her mom was killed and was defiled by this bastard.
So after 20 years, he wouldn’t remember her. He had probably destroyed the lives of countless others ever since then. So Kent, who knew that, was just torturing him out of anger.
It didn’t happen to him, but it happened to someone he loved, and so this bastard will know just how dangerous a dragon can be when he is furious.

60 minutes passed, and Turyn was electrocuted 30 different times. His body was now littered with burnt marks. He has even lost his voice from screaming since he had screamed his heart out for who knows how long.
"You know, I never truly expected you to know who I was talking about. You wouldn’t even remember her if it had only been a year, let alone 20 years.

But the fact that you, son of a bitch, laid hands on her and even killed her mother—I promise you, until she drives her sword through your heart, I will make it my daily routine to torture you and keep doing it for who knows how long.

In here, you won’t die even if you want to. Hunger won’t kill you, but you will feel it. Thirst won’t kill you either, but you will feel it. So, do well to remember the pain and anguish you will endure.

The lady you destroyed has now made a life for herself because she was strong. She could have ended it all like many you dump in the gutter, but she chose to keep going. And you wanna know why? It was because she wanted to one day kill you.
"I will make it happen, and when the time comes, you will know that in this life, not everybody can be touched—certainly not somebody I love."

Kent blasted him with another dose of lightning, snuffing him out for the time being. He would wake up a day later to the sound of bats—now multiplied in number—each exacting revenge on the bastard who had touched what he shouldn’t have.
After the torture session, Kent left the prison in a renewed mood. He would be delivering Turyn to his lover a few days before the auction. For now, he would keep torturing him.
"Gaia, did you record what I asked for?" Kent asked.
[Yes]

"Good. I will ask one of Elsa’s Sentinels to deliver it to his parents. They have to know the errors of their ways and the role they played in raising such a scum," Kent said, taking a recording token from Gaia.
He stored it away and was about to enter the alchemy tower to try and concoct a Tier 3 pill when Saintess Selene suddenly contacted him through the connection between them.
"Kent, we have a problem," she said with a grim expression on her face.
"What seems to be the problem?" Kent asked.

"Pill Saint Riva and her disciple are here, and they are after your head. The Gate Master is calming them down, but from the way things are going, the sect might get into trouble," Saintess Selene said.
"Is that so? Then why don’t you tell the Gate Master to relax? I will handle it." Kent smiled and disappeared back to the real world.

"Now, I will ask again, and you would have to do well to remember," Kent said, looking coldly at Turyn.
"Now I dare ask, do you know anyone by the name Alina?" Kent asked again, but Turyn didn’t seem to recall who he was talking about.
"Please let me go.
I don’t know who you are talking about," He said, but Kent only extended his finger, and a bolt of lightning bombarded the bastard.
"You can either keep quiet and recall the faces and names of all the ladies you have defiled and destroyed all for your canal pleasures.
People like you don’t deserve to have easy endings.
So take your time, for you have a lot of those.
I will just be here asking every two minutes, and until you manage to give me a good answer, prepare to receive a blast.
And don’t worry, you won’t die from the lightning.
That will be mercy, so take your time, for the more time you waste, the more chances I will have to torture you."
Kent leaned back on his chair while he observed Turyn, who was groaning with a few burnt skin here and there.
Ken wasn’t making things easy on him.
Two minutes later, another painful groan filled the prison cell.
It was two minutes later and he still hadn’t recall who Alina was.
In truth, Kent knew he wouldn’t be able to remember Alina, considering the issue with her that had happened 20 years ago.
Alina was just 18 when her mom was killed and was defiled by this bastard.
So after 20 years, he wouldn’t remember her.
He had probably destroyed the lives of countless others ever since then.
So Kent, who knew that, was just torturing him out of anger.
It didn’t happen to him, but it happened to someone he loved, and so this bastard will know just how dangerous a dragon can be when he is furious.
60 minutes passed, and Turyn was electrocuted 30 different times.
His body was now littered with burnt marks.
He has even lost his voice from screaming since he had screamed his heart out for who knows how long.
"You know, I never truly expected you to know who I was talking about.
You wouldn’t even remember her if it had only been a year, let alone 20 years.

But the fact that you, son of a bitch, laid hands on her and even killed her mother—I promise you, until she drives her sword through your heart, I will make it my daily routine to torture you and keep doing it for who knows how long.
In here, you won’t die even if you want to.
Hunger won’t kill you, but you will feel it.
Thirst won’t kill you either, but you will feel it.
So, do well to remember the pain and anguish you will endure.
The lady you destroyed has now made a life for herself because she was strong.
She could have ended it all like many you dump in the gutter, but she chose to keep going.
And you wanna know why?
It was because she wanted to one day kill you.
"I will make it happen, and when the time comes, you will know that in this life, not everybody can be touched—certainly not somebody I love."
Kent blasted him with another dose of lightning, snuffing him out for the time being.
He would wake up a day later to the sound of bats—now multiplied in number—each exacting revenge on the bastard who had touched what he shouldn’t have.
After the torture session, Kent left the prison in a renewed mood.
He would be delivering Turyn to his lover a few days before the auction.
For now, he would keep torturing him.
"Gaia, did you record what I asked for?" Kent asked.
[Yes]
"Good.
I will ask one of Elsa’s Sentinels to deliver it to his parents.
They have to know the errors of their ways and the role they played in raising such a scum," Kent said, taking a recording token from Gaia.
He stored it away and was about to enter the alchemy tower to try and concoct a Tier 3 pill when Saintess Selene suddenly contacted him through the connection between them.
"Kent, we have a problem," she said with a grim expression on her face.
"What seems to be the problem?" Kent asked.
"Pill Saint Riva and her disciple are here, and they are after your head.
The Gate Master is calming them down, but from the way things are going, the sect might get into trouble," Saintess Selene said.
"Is that so?
Then why don’t you tell the Gate Master to relax?
I will handle it." Kent smiled and disappeared back to the real world.

chapters.title: Chapter 216: Arrogance is Bliss (1)
paragraphs: At the entrance of the Divine Palace Sect, the wicked Poison Witch and her disciple Annabelle stand with frowns on their faces.
Annabelle was hugging her master’s arm with a frown and a smug expression on her face. Kent wasn’t around, so she frowned.
Gate Master Mara, Camilla, and Ezra are also present, along with the Gate Master from the Alchemy Gate, Old Hans. He is there because a Saint Alchemist is present.
As for the three others, they were initially there to welcome the Pill Saint. However, they are now trying to calm her down as she demands that they bring out the purple-haired brat.
The only purple-haired brat in the sect is Kent, who has already cemented his reputation as a troublemaker extraordinaire.

Nobody knew what had happened, but right now, the Pill Saint—who, even if the Sect Master were present, wouldn’t dare be disrespected—was demanding Kent. And from the look in her eyes, she wasn’t here to thank him.

"I don’t have all day. Bring out this brat who dares to disrespect my honour, or your sect will face the consequences," Pill Saint Riva said, looking directly at Gate Master Mara, who was sweating down to her feet.
She wasn’t about to act all high and mighty. No, she knew when to be arrogant and when to recognize that the odds were against her.
If this were a Sword Sage, she wouldn’t have that panicked look in her eyes. After all, she was a Sword Sage herself.
But Alchemists are different. They don’t follow the same power system. A Grandmaster Pill Master holds more authority than a sect elder or even a sect leader. The reason is that Alchemists are rare.

It’s not an easy profession, so not many can venture into it. Of course, if you’re looking for a Pill Master, you can find thousands, but when searching for Pill Grandmasters and Saints, that number is severely limited.
So, while she may be a Sword Sage—someone highly respected—in front of one of the Seven Pill Saints and the Wicked Poison Witch no less, she was a nobody.
Perhaps only a Sword King could rival that.
"Pill Saint Riva, please give us some time. The disciple in question was in seclusion, so bringing him out will take some time," Gate Master Mara said politely.
She had already sent people to inform the Sword Saintess to bring Kent. While she knew things might escalate at any moment, she did her best to hold Riva back until Kent arrived.
"As I said, I don’t have all day. If he doesn’t appear within the next 10 minutes, I will not hesitate to turn this place into a poison cemetery," Riva declared.
The four gate masters shuddered at her words. Of course, these were not mere threats. She indeed had the power to do exactly as she said, which was why they reacted the way they did.

While she may be a Pill Saint, she was also a poison cultivator—someone with high mastery in using poison and soul attacks. She could easily turn the sect into a wasteland, and she would not hesitate to do so.
Why?
Because there wouldn’t be anyone willing or audacious enough to stop her. In fact, if she wanted, she could kill everyone, and there wouldn’t be much penalization from anyone. She is that powerful.
Perhaps too powerful for anyone’s good.
A couple of minutes into the ten-minute window, Saintess Selene appeared and whispered something into Riva’s ear, causing her eyes to widen.
In her mind, everything was done for her.
Kent had doomed them all.

Kent only told his master to tell the gate master to relax and that he would handle everything. Obviously, from the little he knew about Kent, whatever the purple-haired brat was up to wasn’t something good.
She sighed and looked at the Poison Witch, who had no idea she was about to clash with an equally poisonous bastard.
Nine minutes passed, and they could only stand there and stare at each other. Kent was a no-show, and the Poison Witch was getting impatient.
That was especially true for her disciple, who was doing a minute countdown. One had to hate her, no matter her background or status.

"It seems your sects have forgotten who a Pill Saint is. Today, I will show the entire continent that nobody can mess with a Pill Saint and go scot-free." The moment Anabelle finished the last countdown, the Pill Saint spoke.
She took a step forward, ready to do what she had come there to do. At that moment, hundreds of elders and even disciples were present at the scene.
They had all gathered when word began spreading about the appearance of the Pill Saint.

They had wanted to see her, but now, they all looked scared and ready to run for their lives. None of them, aside from a few elders, the gate masters, and core disciples, could possibly come out of this alive.
"Wait, Pill Saint, this is just a misunderstanding. We can resolve this," Gate Master Mara said, almost pleading.

Though she had forgiven Kent when she found out the sect master was after him, the hatred she had first felt for him resurfaced. And perhaps, this time, she might actually kill him to pacify her anger.
"I have waited enough... This is the outcome of disrespecting my honour." She extended her hand and was about to attack when suddenly, a disciple asked a question.
"If you don’t mind me asking, how did the sect disrespect your honour?"
The question was simple, but the silence that followed was immediate.
A sudden silence descended on the entire space, making everyone turn their heads in the direction the voice came from. They all wanted to see who was bold enough to ask such a question.
Turning, they all saw a purple-haired bastard with his hands clasped behind him, looking in the direction of the Pill Saint, who stood there looking back at him.
Kent had made his appearance, and with it, a sudden quietness filled the space.
"Master, that is him... That is the brat who took the Dreamshade Flowers from me."

chapters.title: Chapter 217: Arrogance is Bliss (2)
paragraphs: "Master, that is him... That is the brat who took the Dreamshade Flowers from me," Annabelle spoke like an overly privileged, arrogant Karen who had too much time on her hands.
The Gate Masters and every disciple turned to Kent, who was standing like he had no care in the world.
"You said you were going to destroy the sect because they disrespected your honor, so why don’t you tell us how they’ve done it?" Kent repeated his question, showing no signs of fear.
The Poison Pill Saint stared at him.
The Gate Masters wore pale expressions.
The disciples all stared, disbelieving.
A mere inner area disciple just questioned the decision of a Pill Saint; that is just too much to handle at the moment.
"You dare question me?" The poison, being conjured, hurled toward Kent, but he just smirked and appeared on the opposite side of where he had stood.

"The last time I met your disciple, she was after a flower I picked and paid for with my own money. I refused to give it to her, not because she wasn’t pretty enough, but because I needed it," Kent said, taking a step forward.
"I bought the herb because I needed it. She was in the wrong here for trying to force her status as the disciple on me. That is just plain stupid, and you know it," Kent added.
"Are you calling my disciple stupid?" the woman asked, looking very angry.
She is the Pill Saint, the most respected, yet a mere bug was questioning her. That was just too much.

"All I did was buy something using my hard-earned money. I didn’t steal from her, nor did I take it from her. I bought it like how everyone else buys, so how does that affect the sect, and what gave you the authority to threaten to destroy an entire sect?"
This time, the question was harsh, but everyone who heard it instantly understood what all this was about. Many began raising their eyebrows, now knowing why the sect was in danger to begin with.
"You know what you did, so stop spouting nonsense," Annabelle said, not even allowing her master to say anything.
"You can shut up, young lady. The adults are talking," Kent said, not even sparing her a glance.
"Tell me, Pill Saint. What is the first rule of alchemy? I know you are a Pill Saint, so the rules are something you may have forgotten.
But the first rule, that I am sure you never forgot. After all, if you forget that rule, then where is your integrity?" Kent asked, and the Pill Saint froze.
This caused a few elders and the Alchemy Gate Master to look at him in shock.
"The path of alchemy is sacred; it must be cherished and should never be looked down upon," Kent said the rule, and the Pill Saint couldn’t move her body.
It wasn’t that there was an invisible force preventing it; it was the fact that she understood where Kent was going.

"An alchemist is to be respected. An alchemist is to be cherished... But this cannot be transferred to other people. You may be a saint with a diamond badge, but you don’t have the authority to give that authority to someone else.

Your disciple tried using your badge. If I were some ignorant child, I would have conceded and even offered an apology, but as a fellow alchemist who cherishes the craft at heart, I have to say that I am really disappointed in you, Pill Saint.
You not only violated the first rule of alchemy, but you also allowed your disciple to run rampant and suppress people with your badge of honor.
If anything, it should be you offering an apology to the sect for threatening them when, in fact, you are the one in the wrong here."
Kent spoke those words with a calm expression, but he was uncertain how it would all pan out. Right now, the Pill Saint was very quiet. She wasn’t making any movement to retort to Kent.
She was listening, and from the look on her face, she seemed to have undergone some self-evaluation.
"All I did was know the rules and follow them. I did not trample on your dignity, nor did I choose to come against you in hopes of angering you.

If anything, you should blame yourself for giving such authority to a mere kid who knows nothing about anything. The path of alchemy is sacred. I may have been gentle today, but there won’t be a next time."

With his hands clasped behind him, Kent began moving back to the sect like a deity. He had said what needed to be said, and now, he could only leave. The rest would depend on what decision the Pill Saint made.
Kent only took ten steps when a sudden force descended on his body, stopping him in his tracks. His body immediately felt heavy, and he started feeling drowsy.
’I have been poisoned,’ he thought, feeling the poison move toward his heart.
"The last time I checked, I am the highest authority here. Who are you to think you can lecture me on alchemy? You have disrespected my badge, and as such, you will pay with your life."
Pill Saint Riva said, causing everyone gathered to take a step back when they noticed Kent’s skin starting to turn red. The poison was lethal and acted very quickly.
Saintess Selene turned pale, and a sword appeared in her hand, but Gate Master Mara held her back, not allowing even her fingers to move.
In her eyes, Kent was as good as dead. It was quite unfortunate, really.
Though he was hateful, he had also made the sect more lively in the few days he had been with them. It would be a shame if he were to die.

The disciples who had come there to watch, though panicking, all seemed to understand something. The Pill Saint, though unreasonable, was actually abusing her status as an Alchemist. They just didn’t know how to voice it.
Kent was the only one who could do that, but even he was currently not in a position to speak.
"How unfortunate. I really wanted this to go well. Too bad it had to result in violence..."
Well, they always say fake it until you can make it

chapters.title: Chapter 218: Arrogance is Bliss (3)
paragraphs: One had to say, the happiest person in the world at the moment was Annabelle.
Her master was giving her exactly what she wanted.
Kent was currently on his knees, his face and skin red, slowly taking on a darker shade of crimson. His body was going through some pain.
Though he refused to scream.
But his body was enduring it, and the external display was just to her satisfaction. Because of Kent, she had never had a good night’s sleep.
All she wanted was to get back at him for disrespecting her. And so, though she wasn’t expecting Kent to be this daring, the current predicament he was in was also good.
It was satisfying...until it wasn’t.
"How unfortunate. I really wanted this to go well. Too bad it had to result in violence..."
Kent spoke, then slowly raised his hand and snapped his fingers.
Immediately, the snapping sound was heard, and his red skin returned to its original glossy tone.
He no longer looked like an over-spiced barbecue. He was back to himself, and it shocked the Pill Saint speechless.
As for Annabelle, she wore a shocked expression at first, but it was quickly replaced by the sudden cold press of a blade against her neck.
It happened so fast that almost no one except Kent saw the 3-meter-tall metallic swordsman appear and press its sword to her neck.
Annabelle now stood pale, a sword pressed against her neck, with the metallic battle drone Kent had bought from the tower standing behind her.
"I really wanted this to end well... I truly did, but now, I’m forced to do this," Kent said, making the doll take a purple talisman with a red dot on it and pressing it against Annabelle’s forehead.
It dissolved into her body, and the doll released her before vanishing.
It took only a couple of seconds, but it was over.

"That is a Life Knot Talisman. I have tied her life to mine. If something happens to me, she will experience the same. If I die, she will also die. This means that if you were to kill me now, you would lose your disciple.

Now, I don’t know how much you care for her, but if I were to guess, she is someone you cannot afford to lose. So, take this as a win. I will free her in three months’ time. If, after three months, you still wish to confront me, then we can fight.
But today, I have other things to worry about, and you and your disciple are not among them."
Kent smiled and gave her the peace sign before blinking away. He appeared 1 kilometer away and then vanished. He didn’t enter the tower, nor did he run away. He simply disappeared.
Obviously, Kent wasn’t done.
But what was he planning, and what was his end game? That was left to be decided by the Pill Saint...
As expected, nobody made a move nor even tried to say anything. Everyone was frozen in place and it was all because of what had happened.
The next second, Kent was dying and then the next, he was fine and linked the disciple of an entire Pill Saint to his life. That was bold and cold as fuck...
"You are his master, right?" This, of course, didn’t have to end in peace.
The Pill Saint looked toward the Sword Saint and her eyes turned cold. Saintess Selene felt her gaze and tightened her grip on her sword.
However, she didn’t even have to do anything. That was because the next second, a rather powerful aura descended on the place, causing everyone to bend their knees.
The Gate masters weren’t spared either.
"If you laid a single finger on her hair, I will kill you where you stand and be damn with your status as the pill saint. I will not let you hurt my sister...Not on my watch"
Spear Saintess Neomi appeared and everyone was shocked yet again. This time, even the pill Saint was shocked.

She had felt her presence and her killing intent, and she knew if she were to do something at the moment, she would regret it. The intent directed toward her was just not something she could underestimate.
"Let’s go, Selene,"
Saintess Selene was released by the Tower Master, who was already shielding her. Selene flew toward her sister, who took her hand, and they flew away together.
They landed 3 kilometers away and turned back to see the Pill Saint staring at them. Nobody just expected something like this to happen.
Even Kent didn’t see this happening since his sudden disappearance was the plan he had cooked up. He knew the Wicked Witch would target his master, so he was counting on that.
Too bad the Spear Saintess ruined his plans. But Kent wasn’t about to put tails on the Saintess...He had to use his next best bullet since the first one misfired.
Suddenly, a voice filled with ridicule echoed throughout the space.
"This was unexpected. Though I never anticipated the Spear Saintess to appear, I did expect you, a full-fledged Pill Saint, to retaliate. Well, what can you expect from someone who is dying anyway?"
Kent’s words were laced with mockery, but to the Pill Saint, they were a shock. In fact, she immediately felt her deepest secret exposed, and not in the way she had ever anticipated.
She wanted to respond, but she couldn’t retort against Kent’s arrogant words.

’You will be dead within 2 years if you aren’t cured. Now, you can keep being a bitch and die young or go back and visit me again after the Pill Master competition. I might just have a way to cure you.’
He said to her telepathically using an item he bought from the Tower shop.
Kent, who was standing in an invisible bubble that he had spent 100,000 tower points on smirked.
In his hand is a disc-shaped item he was about to use to kill the Pill Saint. Luckily, Saintess Neomi appeared and saved her life.
He never wanted her to leave, he was just waiting for her to do something that will validate him attacking.
He used the [Rule Breaker] skill he received from his master when he added her to the harem to cancel her poison abilities for the day.
But if she were to attack again using a non-poison ability, he was ready to use the [Ten thousand Soul Piercing Needle disc].
This was the trump card he had prepared, and it was also the only way he planned on sending the Pill Saint on her way to the afterlife.
Spending a million Tower Points in it guaranteed she would die the moment he used it... It was always better to handle your enemies early before they become torn on your side.
But sometimes too, it’s better to take a step back and take things again.

The gibberish he said about her dying, though, was true; he never planned on using it. But because the spear saintess was now involved, he saw it best to handle it in a more civilized way - by blackmailing her...
’See you around Pill Saint...This is not over.’

sentences.text: One had to say, the happiest person in the world at the moment was Annabelle.
Her master was giving her exactly what she wanted.
Kent was currently on his knees, his face and skin red, slowly taking on a darker shade of crimson.
His body was going through some pain.
Though he refused to scream.
But his body was enduring it, and the external display was just to her satisfaction.
Because of Kent, she had never had a good night’s sleep.
All she wanted was to get back at him for disrespecting her.
And so, though she wasn’t expecting Kent to be this daring, the current predicament he was in was also good.
It was satisfying...until it wasn’t.
"How unfortunate.
I really wanted this to go well.
Too bad it had to result in violence..."
Kent spoke, then slowly raised his hand and snapped his fingers.
Immediately, the snapping sound was heard, and his red skin returned to its original glossy tone.
He no longer looked like an over-spiced barbecue.
He was back to himself, and it shocked the Pill Saint speechless.
As for Annabelle, she wore a shocked expression at first, but it was quickly replaced by the sudden cold press of a blade against her neck.
It happened so fast that almost no one except Kent saw the 3-meter-tall metallic swordsman appear and press its sword to her neck.
Annabelle now stood pale, a sword pressed against her neck, with the metallic battle drone Kent had bought from the tower standing behind her.
"I really wanted this to end well...
I truly did, but now, I’m forced to do this," Kent said, making the doll take a purple talisman with a red dot on it and pressing it against Annabelle’s forehead.
It dissolved into her body, and the doll released her before vanishing.
It took only a couple of seconds, but it was over.
"That is a Life Knot Talisman.
I have tied her life to mine.
If something happens to me, she will experience the same.
If I die, she will also die.
This means that if you were to kill me now, you would lose your disciple.
Now, I don’t know how much you care for her, but if I were to guess, she is someone you cannot afford to lose.
So, take this as a win.
I will free her in three months’ time.
If, after three months, you still wish to confront me, then we can fight.
But today, I have other things to worry about, and you and your disciple are not among them."
Kent smiled and gave her the peace sign before blinking away.
He appeared 1 kilometer away and then vanished.
He didn’t enter the tower, nor did he run away.
He simply disappeared.
Obviously, Kent wasn’t done.
But what was he planning, and what was his end game?
That was left to be decided by the Pill Saint...

Everyone was frozen in place and it was all because of what had happened.
The next second, Kent was dying and then the next, he was fine and linked the disciple of an entire Pill Saint to his life.
That was bold and cold as fuck...

The Pill Saint looked toward the Sword Saint and her eyes turned cold.

chapters.title: Chapter 219: Just who is this Kid
paragraphs: The plan was to come apprehend the brat that disrespected her disciple and ultimately went against the authority of her as the pill saint through her alchemy badge.
But it didn’t go as planned.
First, she got lectured by a brat who knows only one thing: cause trouble.
Then, her one true disciple was hexed by the brat she was after rendering her incapable of attacking him even if she wanted to.
Then, she was threatened by a mere Spear Saintess, which shook her to the bones. The aura displayed by the Spear saintess was just too much for her to do anything.
But that was a bad move on the saintess’s side. The fact that she had the power to threaten her doesn’t mean she hadn’t just put herself in the future crossfire of the Pill Saint.
Luckily, Kent wasn’t done, and thanks to his discovery, the Pill Saint not only became wary of him, but she might have just found herself in a rather unscrupulous situation.
She will remain weak in front of Kent for as long as he wants.
Basically, she came to humiliate and perhaps destroy, but it all backfired on her.
Now, standing at the entrance of the Divine Palace sect, surrounded by thousands of disciples, is the Pill Saint, popularly known as the Wicked Poison Witch...and her pale, arrogant disciple.

She was now staring at the Gate Masters, specifically the Sword Gate Master Mara, who was still not relaxed. The Wicked Poison Witch was still around, so the last thing she would do was remain relaxed.
The sect came this close to getting destroyed, and as it stood, there was yet another chance it might actually be the case.
Luckily for them, the Poison Witch loves her disciple so much that she wouldn’t dare try to put her life in danger.
Kent’s in the sect, so if she tries anything funny, who is to say what the life connection between her and Kent entails?
It could be that there are many things that will come into play, like Kent actually having the power to kill her anytime he wants.
She cannot risk it.
Now, she is being tied down by just a simple human who has just entered the Root Saint stage. It just doesn’t make sense.
"I will be leaving today. There won’t be a next time," the Wicked Poison Witch said before taking her disciple’s hand. The next second, they were surrounded by a mist of poison, and they vanished.
It was after they were gone that everyone could breathe a sigh of relief. The Gate master, elders, and disciples around all heave a sigh of relief...
Then it hit them...
"Just who is that kid... How can he be so composed and even question a Pill Saint like she was her equal? And it is the Wicked Poison Witch no less?" a disciple wondered, making a few others nod.
"You’re asking the wrong question," another disciple joined in. "He was clearly poisoned for a minute there, so just how was he able to suddenly recover?"
This question was actually the right one, as many began speculating.
Kent had indeed been poisoned for a minute, so how was he able to handle the poison and not only survive but also appear as if he had never been in danger to begin with?
"I saw him do something similar about a week ago. It was when the Gate Master tried suppressing him. He just snapped his fingers, and it was like everything coming from the Gate Master was canceled,"
Another disciple said, and once again, many entered a contemplative state.
"Does that mean he has a skill that can cancel anything—from debuffs to poisons and even the aura of a Root Transcendent?"
This question was like a wake-up call to many.
A few of them were there when Kent first arrived at the sect with his master and was stopped by the gate master. They could clearly tell the gate master was suppressing him.
It was visible in the sudden change that appeared on Kent’s face and his master’s back then. But to those who witnessed it, they could tell it wasn’t that simple.
Kent not only changed all of a sudden; it was as if he had rendered the gate master useless in an instant.
Now, they saw a similar thing, and people began making wild assumptions.
"If he can truly cancel everyone’s abilities, then wouldn’t that make him the most dangerous person in the world?" a disciple almost screamed his heart out.
"I don’t think it’s that simple."
"How so? We clearly saw him turn from pale to red, and then, with just a snap of his fingers, he returned to his handsome pale self. How do you explain that?"
"That... I don’t have an explanation now, but I don’t think he can just render anyone useless in front of him. There has to be a limit to his ability."
"I mean, if he can take away or entirely block someone from using their abilities, wouldn’t that be just too much for a single person?"
"True. There has to be a limit."
"But... and this is a long but. But what if there isn’t a limit, and he can actually turn anyone in front of him into a banana?"
"Then that means the entire world would now try to learn this ability of his, or perhaps... you know."
The disciples fall silent as they suddenly reach that spot.
It has only been a few minutes since the altercation, but word has already started reaching thousands. Soon, the news will spread beyond the sect’s walls, already making its way to the outside world.

People will come to know of the disciple in the Divine Palace Sect who has the ability to cancel out even poisoning. Then, they will learn that it has already been used twice—and it worked like magic.
Since that is the case, greed will begin to surface, driving people to seek him out and try to buy his ability.
But when they realize he won’t comply, they will try to kill him—after all, having such a wildcard around would do them no good.
If he were ever used against them, how else would they deal with it?
"And what the fuck is that magnificent yet terrifying look metal that appeared for a couple of seconds..."
"That..."
"Who the fuck is this kid."

chapters.title: Chapter 220: The Second Chain Quest, Great Friends
paragraphs: While everyone was speculating about the true nature of Kent’s abilities, he was on his way to the Spear Gate to see his master.

She had been put in a dangerous situation because of him, and he wanted to make sure she was okay. Of course, she had been fine helping Kent kill the Pill Saint, as that was the safest course of action.
But now that she had nearly been targeted, he felt the need to apologize and, perhaps, take her back to the Sword Gate for a private session.
When he arrived at the Spear Gate, he quickly went to Saintess Neomi’s residence, where his master and her sister were seated under a tree.
"You’re here," Saintess Neomi said, looking strangely at Kent. Today, there was no trace of annoyance in her gaze. It was unusual, in a way.
"Yes, I am here. Thank you for saving my master. Though I expected something like this, I never expected it to be this dangerous," Kent said with a grateful expression.
His master was strong, but in his eyes, she was as delicate as a flower. He didn’t want to put her life in danger.
"I have to give it to you, kid; you have more courage than any other man I’ve met in this life," Saintess Neomi said, and Kent simply smiled.
"That means a lot to me," he replied, placing both palms on his chest and giving a gentle bow. This action caused both his master and her sister to smirk at his antics.
"But what happened? How were you able to suppress everyone? It’s not like you’re now a Spear Sage. You clearly are a Spear Saint, so how were you able to even suppress the gate masters?" Kent asked.
All the happenings around him were canceled when he entered the invisibility bubble.
This allowed him to see clearly what had occurred when the Saintess appeared, and that was how he noticed the Gate Masters were even suppressed to a certain extent.
If that was the case, then how was that possible?
It just doesn’t make any sense here.
"It’s thanks to you, I guess," Saintess Neomi replied.
"How so? I don’t remember the last time I helped you," Kent asked, looking skeptical. He knew she had entered seclusion after their duel, but he didn’t know why that was.

"For some reason, the intent you exuded during our duel made me gain enlightenment, and it wasn’t the normal kind. This was different. In a way, after I woke up, I got a huge boost in my mastery over spear qi and intent."
Saintess Neomi said, making both Kent and his master look at her in their own way.

[What she said is true, Master. She has indeed gone through an enlightenment. It was an enlightenment that may have lasted for a couple of years, which in this case would require her to train a skill or perhaps a technique until her time was up.]
⟪Wait, there’s something like that?⟫ Kent asked. He already knew there were different types of enlightenment; he just didn’t know the specifics.
[Yes. There are quite a few, actually. But if I were to guess, this enlightenment presented her with a technique and a time frame to learn and master it.
There would have been obstacles for her to overcome in order to master the technique and perhaps a decade of time for her to spend inside the enlightenment.
It can be just a few hours on the outside, but on the inside, decades or even centuries can pass. If you gain something inside, it will manifest on the outside. That’s how it was designed.]
⟪Good for her, I guess,⟫ Kent said, looking at the Spear Saintess and smiling.
"Congratulations, then. You are gradually on the track to becoming a Spear Sage at this point," Kent smiled.
His master also nodded. "Congratulations, Big Sister. I would be very happy if I had half your talent."

"Don’t say things like that, Selene. You are much more talented than you think," Saintess Neomi said, holding her hand and bringing a smile to her face, though Kent could tell she wasn’t really smiling.

Because of her low-grade spirit root, she wasn’t at the stage where she could be classified as a genius among her peers. In fact, had it not been for Saintess Neomi, she probably wouldn’t have been admitted into the sect.
Back then, she didn’t meet the requirements to join the sect, but she insisted that if she wasn’t allowed in, then she wouldn’t join either.
Obviously, they wouldn’t want to lose a Platinum-grade spirit root disciple, so they accepted Selene.

Thankfully, because of this generosity from her sister, the Sword Saintess poured her heart into her cultivation of the sword. She had read that the sword’s path doesn’t necessarily require a strong cultivation base.
Since she lacked that, she decided to make up for it with sheer determination, and it paid off. However, she was still not satisfied with her talent.
Kent could only sigh. He had a way to help her and would give it to her soon.
"By the way, Saintess, since I’ve helped you, do I qualify to spend some quality time with your disciple?" Kent asked.
"If you must, go through me first to get to my disciple," Saintess Neomi declared, making Kent smile.
’Oh, I will go through you alright... I’ll go inside you soon enough,’ he thought with a smile.
Immediately after he made that comment, he heard a *ding*, signaling that the universe and the tower had come together to hand him a quest.
⟪ Second Chain Quest: Become Friends With Spear Saintess Neomi ⟫
⟪ Quest Difficulty: Depends ⟫
-> The spear saintess is close to having another enlightenment. This enlightenment is crucial to her future growth, but she couldn’t achieve it with her own effort.
-> So you must help her.
-> All you have to do is spend time with her. The more time you spend with her, the closer she will ascend to the next Enlightenment.
-> The higher the friendship meter rises, the closer she gets to having her next crucial enlightenment. [Estimated: 40/100%]
⟦Friendship Meter: 18/100% ⟧
⟪ Rewards: ⟫
→ 500,000 Tower Points
→ +20% to Friendship Meter
→ Random Item Bingo Card
’Looks like things will soon go my way, I guess.’ Kent smiled but didn’t say anything. For now, she can play hard to get.
