paragraphs: The Gravel Arena is one of the most popular arenas in the Spear Gate.

It’s where most battles happen, and it is where Randy is currently standing, his spear firmly in his grip, surrounded by thousands of disciples as they wait for the brat who thinks he can steal their flower.
Kent was late for the duel, and everyone was pissed.
Well...nobody told them the real reason why Kent was late was because Ingrid’s nipples were in his mouth as he sucked on them for over an hour.
Kent was rather enjoying it since Ingrid’s breasts, though not that big, were very attractive for some reason. He couldn’t resist, so he was doing justice to them while she moaned on his lap.
He refrained from entering between her legs, but his hard dick couldn’t be resisted that easily by Ingrid, so she spent the entire time groping it through his pants.
When they were done, Ingrid was out of breath and had to run off to calm herself down for an entire hour. It was also the main reason he was 20 minutes late for the duel.
When he entered the arena, Randy was already showing his might by exuding his Spear Qi and Intent. Kent just casually walked into the arena with his hands clasped behind his back.
"Sorry for being late. I was very busy," Kent said, turning subtly toward Ingrid. It was just a look, but Randy, who saw this, was immediately enraged, causing him to grit his teeth.
Kent just smiled, knowing this battle would be fun.
"Do any of you have anything to say?" an elder asked.
"Prepare to die, bastard," Randy gritted his teeth again, but this time, a potent killing intent appeared in his eyes. He wasn’t happy about the sudden turn of events.
He was supposed to have Ingrid, not this no-name who appeared out of nowhere and started causing too much trouble for everyone.
Kent would have to go if he wanted to have a shot at Ingrid.
"Just give up, Mr. You can’t kill me, nor do you have the balls to make Ingrid your woman, so just give up. Of course, since we are here now, I might as well open your eyes."
Kent extended his hand, and the golden sword sheath appeared, captivating everyone.
"Give it your best shot because this will be the first and only chance you will get to fight me. Make it count," Kent said before gazing at the elder.
"Begin."
The moment he said that Randy unleashed two wide arcs of attack using spear qi. It created two sharp cross arcs that flashed toward Kent with terrifying speed.
They arrived in an instant, but before they could land on Kent, he waved his hand, swinging the golden sheath. The attack was neutralized instantly, but another two followed.

Kent defended equally and even moved to land an attack. But he had to stop when he sensed danger coming from his right. He quickly defended using his sword sheath and then used his foot to kick away a spear thrust coming from Randy.
’So he can use flying weapons, huh?’ Kent muttered with an amused smirk.
Randy controlled the spear, making it attack Kent in the head while he used the original spear to attack from the side.
It was a perfectly coordinated attack that would have been overwhelming had it not been for Randy’s lack of experience.
He was using it as a distraction when he should have made it the killing weapon. Kent saw all this after defending against it just three times.
The Genesis Sword Path he was walking was not that simple.
His understanding of the sword seemed to grow with every battle he fought, and he had fought in hundreds already.
Although only one of those battles was impactful, the rest were also enlightening. Now, Randy was showing something new, and Kent was experiencing it all like a lesson being taught for free.
’He is even trying to defeat me without using any active abilities,’ Kent said to himself and then chose to force him to use some skills, or else he would lose.
Right now, he had seen his strength when he fought against Saintess Neomi, so he wasn’t taking Randy seriously.
It was one of those moments you knew underestimating your opponent was the right thing. Kent has already fought someone who could easily crush Randy.
So, he wasn’t about to overestimate someone like Randy when he lasted 4 whole hours against the Spear Saintess. That would just be plain stupid...
The current him should be fighting his Master’s level talents, not some random Core disciple winning over a girl who doesn’t even like him.
"24 String Weaving Strike."
Kent unleashed the infamous sword skill of the Sword Gate, and Randy was forced back. It was a quick attack that took him by surprise.
"24 String Weaving Strike."
He unleashed it again, and this time, Randy swung his spear in a wide arc. "Spear Beam Arc!"

A wide arc that beamed like a flash of light shot toward Kent, forcing him to take a few steps back. Meanwhile, Randy, now holding twin spears in his hands, realized he was facing a monster, so he, too, had to become a monster.
"Spear Rain." He used the spear to draw a circle in the air, causing a spell diagram to materialize. Then, spears began raining down from it, making everyone watching cheer loudly.
This was one of Randy’s ultimate moves to end a duel. The moment he used this skill, one had to know what was coming next.
Kent defended against the spears, showing no sign of being overwhelmed. However, his focus was on the spears raining down—or so it seemed.
This was, of course, what Randy wanted. He wanted Kent’s focus on the spears while he made his next move...
"Spear to the Infinity." He immediately unleashed another ultimate skill. He threw his spear, which instantly increased in size to several meters and in thickness by several inches.
"Die, bastard," Randy gritted his teeth in anger as he snapped his fingers, bringing forth yet another large spear from the spell diagram in the air.
Two long and deadly spears were heading toward Kent, who just stood there. His hands were clasped behind him as he waited until the attacks were a meter away from him.
Suddenly, a powerful sword qi and intent burst out of Kent’s body, and like cutting paper, both attacks were neutralized down to the smallest detail.
This was a WTF moment for everyone.
They were all gobsmacked. But it didn’t take long for people to start shuddering in fear.
"You are too weak. Go and train for another decade. Perhaps then, you can execute this move perfectly."
After Kent said those words, the rest was a total beatdown that saw him landing all sorts of attacks on Randy, making him scream his heart out.

The pain wasn’t from sword wounds. No, it was from physical attacks using his feet and knees. He broke a couple of Randy’s bones, and when he was done, Randy was still conscious but couldn’t even move his fingers.
Kent didn’t go overboard according to his books, but he also didn’t let him off easy. In the end, everyone could only watch in fear as Kent walked away with Ingrid in his arms.
It was like that phrase: I came, I saw, I conquered.

chapters.title: Chapter 228 - 13th Rakshasa Guard (1)
paragraphs: A few hours before Kent’s battle with Randy, the Spear Saintess, who had been influenced by Kent’s unique aura, rushed to her training room and immediately sat in a lotus posture.
She had gained clarity, and it was all thanks to Kent’s aura.
Before he was sent to the World of Sonox, Kent spent an entire year in the realm of hatred and resentment with Vexthra, the owner of the god realm.
The place was filled with divine energy, which influenced his own aura. He also received the aura of hatred and resentment from Vexthra after adding her to his harem as his first wife.
The aura was that of a goddess, and Kent inherited it.

Of course, this doesn’t mean he could immediately transform into a god capable of unleashing the aura of a deity. No, the aura was undoubtedly powerful, but he wouldn’t even be able to harness just 10% of it at his current level.
He didn’t have the requirements for that.
However, he could, at least, exude an aura that contained traces of divinity. This, in fact, became much more pronounced when he awakened 5% of his Primordial Chaos Dragon bloodline.
Kent still had no idea he was a walking treasure. The Sect Master, an evil practitioner, sensed it and was drawn to it.
The Spear Saintess was also influenced by it during their fight.
So, while he didn’t realize how extraordinary he was, he knew it had helped the Saintess once, and now he was given a way to help her again since she was practically his at the moment.
She sat in a lotus posture for several minutes, meditating.
Then, suddenly, a red runic mark appeared on her forehead, and an unknown force pulled away her soul and consciousness.
The next moment, she appeared in a valley spanning several miles both in front and back. Surrounding her were tall mountains.
From where she stood, she could see thousands of tombstones, each with stairs leading to them. They all appeared to have different colors and emanated different energies.
Saintess Neomi quickly climbed to the one closest to her and gazed at it closely.

⟦Description: Here lies the spirit of Nelani, the Light Menace Spear Monarch, who fought with the Heavenly Ascendance Legion and defeated the Laughing Stalking Demon. If you wish to awaken and claim this Weapon Spirit, add your blood to her tombstone and invoke the challenge.⟧
"W-What? A... a... a Monarch?"
Saintess Neomi’s heartbeat quickened as she read the description on the tombstone, taking a few steps back...
The person was a Monarch in the path of the spear. Just a few steps away from the Legend stage...
In the path of weapon cultivation, there are various stages, levels, or ranks: Novice, Adept, Master, Grandmaster, Saint, Sage, King, Emperor, Monarch, Legend, Divine, God, Supreme, and Celestial.
These are the stages, and the tombstone belonged to someone who had reached the Monarch stage, which was simply unbelievable.
’How can I possibly win against this kind of person?’ she said to herself.
"The last time I checked, I only had one chance and one chance only. If I mess it up, that will be all. I can’t mess this up. I better relax and check out the others first.
If I am not mistaken, fate will certainly play a role in this. I can’t rush it."
The Saintess began descending and ascending as she checked more and more tombstones. Every last one of them was just too good to be true.

⟦Description: Here lies the spirit of Tharok, the Iron Tempest Spear Emperor, who quelled the Raging Storm Titan and forged an empire from the ashes of chaos. To awaken and claim this Weapon Spirit, offer your blood to his tombstone and invoke the challenge.⟧

⟦Description: Here lies the spirit of Zorath, the Voidpiercer Spear Monarch, who sundered the Celestial Chains and banished the Eternal Void Serpent. To awaken and claim this Weapon Spirit, anoint this tombstone with your blood and invoke the challenge.⟧

⟦Description: Here rests the spirit of Draven, the Inferno Spear King, who scorched the armies of the Obsidian Horde and turned the Ashlands into a sea of fire. To awaken and claim this Weapon Spirit, let your blood fall upon his tombstone and invoke the challenge.⟧
She checked dozens of tombstones, and there were still hundreds, if not thousands, more remaining. Saintess Neomi was taking her time to check them all, but her efforts proved to be misguided.
She couldn’t possibly check them all. In fact, she began to grow impatient as she moved from one tombstone to the next.
"Let me take a breather. Until I choose a tombstone, I won’t be sent back," she said to herself, sitting down and beginning to meditate with her eyes closed.

All the spirits she had seen so far were within the Saint to Monarch stage. It was both overwhelming and, in a way, very addicting. She wanted to know their names and research them when she returned to the real world.
Of course, fate and destiny weren’t just sitting idle either...
Two miles from her, a red tombstone marked with a skull began exuding a potent killing aura. It wasn’t the weak aura emitted by those who had fought hundreds of battles.
No, this type of aura could easily kill millions if unleashed.
Suddenly, the energy around it grew even more intense than before as a lady with four arms, red skin, and hair standing on end emerged from the tombstone.
In each hand, she held a spear made from different materials, each with a unique shape. Her eyes were dark, and a dark red aura emanated from them.
She was covered only around her chest and waist, a rather provocative attire, but her terrifying presence left no room for inappropriate thoughts.
She rose and gazed in the direction of the Spear Saintess, her eyes burning hotter than pepper. "Finally," she muttered, sending a strand of blood flying toward Saintess Neomi.

⟦Here lies the spirit of the 13th Guard of Rakshasa. Before her transcendence, Rakshasa left behind 13 keys, each representing a path to the Rakshasa Spear Path.

Here lies the spirit of Narodin, the 13th Guard of Rakshasa, the Blood Spear Monarch.⟧

She had gained clarity, and it was all thanks to Kent’s aura.
Before he was sent to the World of Sonox, Kent spent an entire year in the realm of hatred and resentment with Vexthra, the owner of the god realm.
The place was filled with divine energy, which influenced his own aura.
He also received the aura of hatred and resentment from Vexthra after adding her to his harem as his first wife.
The aura was that of a goddess, and Kent inherited it.
Of course, this doesn’t mean he could immediately transform into a god capable of unleashing the aura of a deity.
No, the aura was undoubtedly powerful, but he wouldn’t even be able to harness just 10% of it at his current level.
He didn’t have the requirements for that.
However, he could, at least, exude an aura that contained traces of divinity.
This, in fact, became much more pronounced when he awakened 5% of his Primordial Chaos Dragon bloodline.
Kent still had no idea he was a walking treasure.
The Sect Master, an evil practitioner, sensed it and was drawn to it.
The Spear Saintess was also influenced by it during their fight.
So, while he didn’t realize how extraordinary he was, he knew it had helped the Saintess once, and now he was given a way to help her again since she was practically his at the moment.
She sat in a lotus posture for several minutes, meditating.
Then, suddenly, a red runic mark appeared on her forehead, and an unknown force pulled away her soul and consciousness.
The next moment, she appeared in a valley spanning several miles both in front and back.
Surrounding her were tall mountains.
From where she stood, she could see thousands of tombstones, each with stairs leading to them.
They all appeared to have different colors and emanated different energies.
Saintess Neomi quickly climbed to the one closest to her and gazed at it closely.
⟦Description: Here lies the spirit of Nelani, the Light Menace Spear Monarch, who fought with the Heavenly Ascendance Legion and defeated the Laughing Stalking Demon.
If you wish to awaken and claim this Weapon Spirit, add your blood to her tombstone and invoke the challenge.⟧
"W-What?
A... a... a Monarch?"
Saintess Neomi’s heartbeat quickened as she read the description on the tombstone, taking a few steps back...
The person was a Monarch in the path of the spear.
Just a few steps away from the Legend stage...
In the path of weapon cultivation, there are various stages, levels, or ranks: Novice, Adept, Master, Grandmaster, Saint, Sage, King, Emperor, Monarch, Legend, Divine, God, Supreme, and Celestial.
These are the stages, and the tombstone belonged to someone who had reached the Monarch stage, which was simply unbelievable.
’How can I possibly win against this kind of person?’ she said to herself.
"The last time I checked, I only had one chance and one chance only.
If I mess it up, that will be all.
I can’t mess this up.
I better relax and check out the others first.
If I am not mistaken, fate will certainly play a role in this.
I can’t rush it."
The Saintess began descending and ascending as she checked more and more tombstones.
Every last one of them was just too good to be true.
⟦Description: Here lies the spirit of Tharok, the Iron Tempest Spear Emperor, who quelled the Raging Storm Titan and forged an empire from the ashes of chaos.
To awaken and claim this Weapon Spirit, offer your blood to his tombstone and invoke the challenge.⟧
⟦Description: Here lies the spirit of Zorath, the Voidpiercer Spear Monarch, who sundered the Celestial Chains and banished the Eternal Void Serpent.
To awaken and claim this Weapon Spirit, anoint this tombstone with your blood and invoke the challenge.⟧
⟦Description: Here rests the spirit of Draven, the Inferno Spear King, who scorched the armies of the Obsidian Horde and turned the Ashlands into a sea of fire.
To awaken and claim this Weapon Spirit, let your blood fall upon his tombstone and invoke the challenge.⟧
She checked dozens of tombstones, and there were still hundreds, if not thousands, more remaining.
Saintess Neomi was taking her time to check them all, but her efforts proved to be misguided.
She couldn’t possibly check them all.

All the spirits she had seen so far were within the Saint to Monarch stage.
It was both overwhelming and, in a way, very addicting.

Of course, fate and destiny weren’t just sitting idle either...
Two miles from her, a red tombstone marked with a skull began exuding a potent killing aura.
It wasn’t the weak aura emitted by those who had fought hundreds of battles.

chapters.title: Chapter 229 - 13th Rakshasa Guard (2)
paragraphs: The blood flew and entered the Saintess’ forehead before she could even comprehend what had happened.
It moved swiftly, entering instantaneously, making it seem as though nothing had occurred.
However, something significant had indeed taken place, for the Saintess was suddenly teleported away, appearing in a place bathed in red light.
It was as if everything there was crafted from the color red. The only non-red entity in that space was Saintess Neomi, who turned back and forth, trying to make sense of her surroundings.
"Where am I?" she asked, but no answer came.
She hovered in the air, looking around more intently, yet still receiving no response despite knowing something had brought her there.
"How did I get here?" she wondered, but again, there was no reply.
She chose to remain silent and focus on understanding the space she was in. Perhaps that would help her if she concentrated. At least, that was what she decided to believe.
So she began to observe her surroundings, but she quickly realized she wasn’t going to find any answers.
The reason was simple: there were no answers to be found. She was inside some kind of dome with no clouds, only a blood-red sea raging below her.
Those were the only two things she could see—and that was all there was to see.
"Welcome to the realm of Rakshasa, oh chosen one. Your trial begins in 5... 4... 3... 2... 1." A voice spoke, counting down. When the countdown struck zero, a figure appeared.
Now, facing the Saintess was a mirror version of herself but with wild, crimson-red eyes.
It all happened so fast that she wasn’t able to say anything. Before she knew it, she was staring into a carbon copy of herself, gazing at her with intense killing intent.
"What the—"
The Saintess was pushed back when a sudden swing landed on her spear. The clone attacked, and the force behind it was overwhelming.
The red sea was still raging below them, but the figure now in front of her made her mind leave the ominous crimson environment she was in and drawn into the battle...
’That is definitely not me, but bring it on,’ she thought, spinning her spear.
The next second, she clashed with the clone again. This time, the force came from both sides, creating a powerful shockwave that pushed them apart.
’She is stronger... stronger than me.’
The Saintess gritted her teeth, her hands tightening around the shaft of her spear as she steadied herself. It wasn’t going to be a battle she could easily win.
The clone stood a few meters away, its crimson eyes glowing like embers in the dark.
Without warning, the clone lunged, its movements a blur of speed and precision.
The Saintess barely had time to raise her spear, deflecting a strike that would have cleaved her in two.
The impact sent a jolt through her arms, but she retaliated swiftly, thrusting her spear toward the clone’s chest.
The clone sidestepped with precise steps, its red eyes never leaving hers. It was like she was reading the Saintess’ every move before she could even make them.
’It’s faster, too,’ she realized, her heart pounding.
The clone attacked again, its spear whirling in a deadly arc.
The Saintess ducked, feeling the rush of air as the weapon narrowly missed her head.
She countered with a sweeping strike aimed at the clone’s legs, but it leaped effortlessly into the air, flipping backward and landing with perfect balance.
’Wait. That is something I will do. Hold on, does this mean the clone is me...a better me?’ The saintess didn’t like the feeling.
They’d been fighting for a few minutes now, and at every swing, the clone seemed to know what she was about to do.
Also, whenever the clone attacks, the Saintess feels a sense of déjà vu. It was as if she saw herself do that, which now made it clear the clone was her.
A better her.

It had her skills, techniques, way of adapting in battle, and the next move to use in combat. It even went as far as knowing what she would do when an attack was halted mid-strike and switched to a different one.
And to top it off, the clone was doing it better than her. That could only mean she had now entered a battle against a perfect version of herself.
’I am screwed.’
The red sea roared below, waves crashing against an unseen shore. The Saintess used the momentary pause to catch her breath, her mind racing.
’It has my moves, my strength, but amplified. How do I fight something that knows me better than I know myself?’
There was no answer to be found.
All she could do now was follow the algorithm and keep doing what she would do in this situation, but be hyper-aware of when to double down since she knew how brilliant she was.
The battle was not something she could easily win.
Why?
It was because the Saintess was devious and cunning in battle. This also means the clone has copied her cunningness and is now using it against her.
’Just one chance, else I will lose this... But I never asked for this, so what is going on?’ She thought for a moment and then resolved herself.
"You know the saying: When it looks, appears, and behaves like you, then you just have to forget yourself and be yourself," Saintess Neomi smiled and then moved.

She thrust her spear forward, kicked out, moved her craft arm to the left, and then blew an air forward from her mouth. It was a perfected, coordinated random attack with the spear, leg, arm and mouth.
The spear was saved, the kick was blocked, and the arm was caught, but the air wasn’t blocked. This caused the clone to close her eyes momentarily.
’Got your ass.’
The Saintess smirked as she let go of the spear and held onto the clone’s face. "In the end, being human is always the best."
She pressed hard, gripping the clone’s face. The grip around her face was so tight that the clone’s eyes popped out, and then—
"Squash."
The clone’s head burst apart, ending her.
’And that is how you kill a better version of yourself. Just be yourself.’ She sighed, and then she felt her surroundings start to change.
A few seconds later, her surroundings shifted, and she appeared in front of the four-armed lady, who was now kneeling like a servant to her master.
"You’ve passed my test. It’s now time to form the contract..."
Saintess Neomi smiled, but she didn’t sing her heart out just yet. Until she was back inside her real body, she wasn’t about to celebrate.
’I have succeeded, and from the look of things, she is also a Monarch. I guess my chances of becoming a Sage and the rest are guaranteed now.’ She was happy.
Of course, what she doesn’t know is that while she had somehow managed to become the master of the 13th Rakshasa Guard, it wasn’t because of her fate alone.
No, the universe favored her through somebody, and it was also because of this favor that would follow her around now.

She had just taken a Rakshasa Guard as a weapon spirit, and soon, she would be receiving the 4th Primordial Spear Path, known as the Deadly Spears of Rakshasa—the path walked by one of the Seven Heavenly Supremes who entered reincarnation eons ago.

chapters.title: Chapter 230: First Tier Three Pill Concoction
paragraphs: After the duel with Randy, Kent spent a few hours with Ingrid before leaving to return to the Sword Gate.
He told her he was going into seclusion for about a week, so when he came out, he would visit her and her master, who would not be emerging from her own seclusion for the next couple of days.
When he got back, he immediately entered the Alchemy Tower, where he went straight to the pill room and prepared for his first attempt at concocting his first Tier 3 pill.
This was one of the requirements he needed to fulfill before he could become a Pill Grandmaster, where true pill-making began.
’Qi Gathering Pill’
That was the pill he was about to make, and it was also the pill he had always tried to create ever since he became an alchemist.

He had chosen it as his go-to pill for when ever he was about to ascend the next stage of alchemy. His understanding was still limited, but he also wasn’t about to assume he was an ordinary alchemist.
He had the Primordial Alchemy records in his mind. This alone was enough to set him apart.

"If I manage to finish this, I can even concoct that pill and let Alina auction it during the Annual Auction. Though it will just be a Tier 3 pill, it will undoubtedly be a perfect pill, something anyone would kill for."
Kent smiled and then started arranging the ingredients into six portions.
He wasn’t about to assume he could easily make a Tier 3 pill. He would need to focus more on understanding his flame and have powerful soul strength to back it up.

If he had these three things, he would also need talent and passion for pill-making. Luckily, Kent had all of these, but he still needed training, which in this case would likely involve burning a few herbs.
After arranging the ingredients, he lit his Blue Void Flame and began heating the furnace. He used the heating technique he had learned to speed up the process.
Kent had mastered some of the techniques in the Primordial Alchemy records, so his efficiency this time was much more impressive.
After the cauldron heated for a few minutes, he tossed in the first ingredient and started the process of burning and extracting the medicinal essence from it.
The process wasn’t as fast as before, mainly because this was a Tier 3 pill herb, and the focus and control required for it were not to be underestimated.
Kent focused on that, and slowly, he started showing signs of understanding something. He added the second herb, and then he began adding the rest.
Twenty minutes later, the last herb was tossed into the cauldron, and the essence was extracted. He then sighed and proceeded to the next step.
He started forming the pill while burning away impurities. This process was also the most tedious, as he had to be careful not to let the flame get too close or too far away.
Doing so would result in burning the pill, which, in this case, was not the best outcome any alchemist would hope for.
This process took close to an hour until, suddenly, Kent began using another technique after the pill was condensed.
This time, he was using a technique to eliminate all the impurities that remained after the pill was condensed but had not yet hardened.
This also meant it was his last chance to remove impurities, given the level of knowledge he had in pill-making.
The records provided everything any Pill Master would want to know in the path of alchemy. So, he was knowledgeable in this aspect.
But even so, he was still lacking, and that was evident, considering he was struggling to handle this simple task...
Close to an hour later, a puff sound escaped the cauldron, indicating the pill had formed, and the process was complete. He opened the cauldron and retrieved the pill.
Gaia was even a step ahead and displayed the details of his first Tier 3 pill concoction.
⟪You have successfully concocted a Qi Gathering Pill. Grade: Tier 3, Quality: Good. Purity: 89%.⟫
"Not bad for my first trial, really," Kent smiled, reading the message.
He decided to try again, determined to improve his results. With each attempt, he focused more intently, applying the knowledge from the records and refining his technique.
On his second attempt, the process felt smoother.
He added the herbs with greater precision, controlled the flame more carefully, and removed impurities more efficiently.
When the pill formed, Gaia displayed the results:
⟪You have successfully concocted a Qi Gathering Pill. Grade: Tier 3, Quality: Excellent. Purity: 96%.⟫
"Better," Kent murmured, pleased with the progress. He took a moment to analyze what he had done differently, then prepared for his third attempt.
"I knew the best option was to master the flame control. It proves to be the best decision I have made, and it’s now paying off quite well..."
Kent smiled and went ahead to give it another shot. Now that he had seen most of his mistakes, he was bound to succeed if nothing went wrong.
This time, he was even more meticulous.
His movements were fluid, and his focus was unwavering.
He adjusted the flame with precision and ensured every impurity was eliminated before the pill hardened.
When the cauldron released its familiar puff, he retrieved the pill, and Gaia’s message appeared:
⟪You have successfully concocted a Qi Gathering Pill. Grade: Tier 3, Quality: Perfect. Purity: 100%.⟫
⟪You have completed the third requirement⟫
Kent’s eyes widened in satisfaction. "A perfect pill," he said, a grin spreading across his face. "This is what I was aiming for. And all I needed was three trials."
"Damn, I am good" Kent was very happy.
The process was now a part of him, allowing him to execute them flawlessly as if he had been practicing alchemy for years.
Feeling confident, he decided to attempt one final time to solidify his mastery. The fourth attempt was flawless, as if everything had fallen into place.
The pill formed effortlessly, and Gaia confirmed his success:
⟪You have successfully concocted a Qi Gathering Pill. Grade: Tier 3, Quality: Perfect. Purity: 100%.⟫
"Since I now have my first to success, why not make it four with the two potions of ingredients remaining?"
Thus, Kent started two more furnaces of pills, which, after 2 hours, saw him holding four Flawless pills in jade bottles.

Then the day came, and he appeared in the arena.
But before the duel, he had to complete a quest, and that quest was to anger the Gate Master and let her aim her killing intent at him.
Kent didn’t suffer much, considering the Gate Master hated him back then because of his arrogance. This led to him and her starting off and continuing on the wrong foot.
But that was just a means to an end, and Kent won.
He also won a pill recipe he could use to make a pill called the Innate Talent Awakening Pill. The Quest reward was very generous...
This recipe was just a sample of a much larger recipe used to make a rather powerful pill of the same name but with different effects.
He must become a Pill King and qualify to make Tier 9 or 10 pills before he can attempt that.
But the Tier 3 version is equally awesome.

As the name suggests, this pill will awaken the innate talent of anyone who takes it. In other words, they will awaken their bloodlines, which will grant them certain aspects and then awaken some innate talents.

But that isn’t all. Innate talents are based on one’s Spirit Root Grade, so even if this pill doesn’t upgrade the spirit root, it will certainly enhance its effects, making the person much more talented.
This means just one pill can transform someone with mediocre talent into a powerhouse capable of rising to the peak.
However, that is the effect of the Tier 9 or 10 pill, which he can only concoct if and when he becomes a Pill King.
For the Tier 3 version, the person will only see an upgrade in their talent, which will be permanent, but it will depend on how talented the person who took it is.
There will be no bloodline awakening.
There will be no innate talent awakening.
And there will be no upgrade of their spirit root.

However, if one’s talent can take them as far as the Root Saint stage, then after taking the pill, they will have the talent to go as far as the Root Great Sage or even step into the Root Transcendent stage.
Root Great Sage is guaranteed.
This means all those stuck at the Root Sage stage for years now can have a chance to move forward. This isn’t a Realm Breakthrough Pill or a Realm Ascension Pill.
It enhances your cultivation talent and allows you to keep going.
Kent retrieved the ingredients he had bought from the Tower.
"I only have one portion of this, so I better do well not to concoct any bad pill," Kent muttered to himself and then resumed heating the cauldron.
’A pill is not a pill if it’s not 100% pure.’
That was what he read on the cover of the Primordial Pill records when he first got them. Now, he understood why.
Why take a pill if you will also accumulate impurities?
It had to be pure, meaning free of impurities, so you could gain all the benefits that came with the pill without any side effects.
"Perhaps I should try impurity removal pills next. Those will sell well, but I do not need the money anyway. I guess I will do it for the fame."
Kent smiled and then tossed the first of 13 ingredients in. He followed up after a couple of minutes by tossing the second in.
He then proceeded with the rest, and in under 30 minutes, the essence was extracted, and he began condensing it while burning away impurities.
He was also doing his best to handle the burning away of too much essence.
"I wonder if one day I can extract the purest form of essence without any impurities in it," he muttered, but he knew it was only a matter of time.
Another thirty minutes later, the pill formed, and now he was burning the last of the impurities. It took a couple of minutes, but he managed to handle that, and then he hardened the pill.
When the puff came, he smiled because Gaia was always ready to tell him whether he failed or not. Right now, even a 99.9% pure pill was a failure to him.
Thankfully, he had the talent for alchemy, too, so he managed to create yet another 100% pure pill for the day—his fifth.
⟪You have successfully concocted an Innate Talent Awakening Pill. Grade: Tier 3, Quality: Perfect. Purity: 100%.⟫
"This will do. It will make people keep talking about me until I make my name known during the Pill Master Competition."
Kent smiled, knowing soon his status would rise by several degrees because he was the only one on the human continent capable of concocting perfect pills.
"I should probably remember my past and see if I can grow from it," he sighed and lay back to catch some sleep because he was tired from the concoctions.
When he woke up, 8 days had passed, but it was only 8 hours on the outside. He quickly freshened up and went to the Tower City to meet Li Hua and the others.
"Big brother, I missed you so much," Li Hua said, jumping into his embrace. She was training with Nyxira, the Umbral Elf, one of Elsa’s three Soul Sentinels.
"You were training, so I didn’t want to disturb you," Kent said, forcing a smile.
"Yes, I’m growing very fast. Master Nyxira said I’m the rarest talent she has ever met, and I have the makings of a dangerous and powerful assassin," Li Hua said, puffing out her chest.
"You are indeed the best. Just don’t give her too much trouble, okay?" Kent set her down.
"Okay, big brother. I’ll keep training nonstop," she said before running away, leaving only Kent with Nyxira, Kael, and Kaelion.
They are the three soul sentinels Elsa currently has under her command.
"I have a mission for you. It’s just a delivery mission, but it must be done in secret," Kent said to Nyxira. She was the assassin and the best suited for the task.
"I will do my best, my lord," Nyxira said, bowing slightly, making Kent scratch the back of his head. It seemed they still wouldn’t call him by his real name.
Elsa had told him that was what they would call him for as long as they remained her Soul Sentinels. Perhaps, if she were to free them and let them have their own identities, it might change.
But she didn’t see that happening, considering no Soul Sentinel would be foolish enough to ask for that, especially not from an Astra Warden, a True Aether Warden.

"Also, you should be ready. In the coming days, someone will be taking you three on a mission where you will do some killing and, perhaps, some major rescue missions, depending on how everything goes."
"We will be ready, my lord," the three responded.
Kent retrieved a jade box worth at least 300,000 spirit stones and handed it to Nyxira. Then, he gave her a map with the residence of the Miller Noble family marked on it.
After giving her some more instructions, the two of them left the tower and appeared somewhere far from the sect.
"When you’re done, use the connection between you and the tower to enter. You won’t have to come here again before entering. You can enter from anywhere," Kent said, and Nyxira nodded.
"Then, see you later."
After parting ways, Kent headed toward Vastport City, where a certain manager was waiting for him to come and rock her world.

’I wonder how monstrous any of these skills will be after upgrading them,’ Kent thought, clenching his fist and wishing for a mission to challenge him to use his strength.
’I fought Saintess Neomi in a controlled environment. I want one that requires me to face death and smile,’ he mused. His determination was already set.
If only he knew the quest pool was already creating a unique quest he could not refuse. In the coming days, Kent would learn why the universe gave him all these gifts through his women.
Twenty minutes after adding Alina to the Harem, Vexthra’s angry tone echoed in Kent’s mind.
"My love, tell me you have captured that brat who hurt my sister," Vexthra demanded.
She was leaking killing intent from where she stood in the god realm. Her gaze was filled with extreme hatred, the kind that emanated from the soul.

Initially, she wanted to tease Alina and even subtly threaten her not to get any funny ideas using her butt to seduce Kent. So, she asked about her background, and Alina, who was scared for a moment, sang like a bird.
Now, Vexthra, who knew what happened to her 20 years ago, was very angry. If Kent’s answer didn’t suit her, she would probably do something crazy.
[Don’t worry. I have already taken care of that brat. I will take Alina to her the moment you are done with her. Now, get to know her, and please be gentle with her. She is fragile.]
"I will, and thank you for putting her first. I will make sure she doesn’t feel left out. For now, I will need a couple of hours with her, if you don’t mind," Vexthra asked, calming down a bit.
[Take all the time you need.]
Kent was actually very angry now that he thought about it. So, he immediately instructed Gaia to take the Battle Doll to the Tower prison.
He would be taking Alina there in 8 hours’ time.
That’s 8 days for Turyn with the Battle Doll.

chapters.title: Chapter 234: The Miller Noble Family
paragraphs: Willow City is one of the major cities in the Varyndor Kingdom.
It was also the city governed by the Miller Family. It used to be called Miller City, but after the 5th head of the Miller family died, the name was changed to Willow City.
A city of beauty and wealth.
But the ones ruling it are scum.
Two months ago, an entire nuclear family was killed, mainly because the oldest daughter of Artisan Kuni was kidnapped in their home by the goons of Turyn, the heir of the Miller family.
They threatened to take it to the authorities, but it was that very act that got them killed. The young lady who was taken away was never heard from again.
A month before that, a similar thing happened. This time, an entire mercenary group was killed, and the vice group leader, who happened to be a beauty, was taken.
But that wasn’t all. There were other incidents, but they were all covered up, and those who could prove otherwise were eliminated.
All this was done by Turyn.
But while his family knew this, they did nothing to stop him. Instead, they always covered his tracks and made sure nobody could do anything to them.
They are supreme.
But their karma has finally caught up to them.
The mission Kent gave Nyxira was a success. She delivered the recording crystal, which contained a note, to the head of the Miller noble family.
In fact, if Nyxira had wanted, she could have assassinated the old bastard, who was asleep with three naked ladies in his arms when she delivered the items.
...Well, she left her mark before leaving.
Who knows when else she would be asked to assassinate him? It was best to leave a mark for the future.
In the morning, when Kiel Miller woke up and saw the jade box, he immediately took it and opened it, only to find a recording crystal that contained a recording of his son getting electrocuted.
The video showed the miserable state his son was in and the kind of pain he was enduring. In fact, Kiel wasn’t even halfway through the video when he started coughing up blood.
His anger was so intense that he began coughing up blood.
The video showed his one and only son, the heir meant to replace him one day. The talented son of the Miller family was now being tortured.
He couldn’t hold himself up any longer, so he fell to the ground along with the note inside the jade box. After a couple of minutes on the ground, he picked up the note and began to read.
⟪Greetings. If you are reading this, then your son Turyn is dead. No need to cry about it. But yes, he is dead, for you saw this coming many years ago and did nothing about it.
Now, while I would love to gloat about it, I don’t have time, so listen carefully, for the survival of the entire Miller family depends on it.
I know everything about you. I know what you like and dislike, I know the kind of women you are into, and I know the kind of person you are. You are the scum of a father, by the way.
But that is just by the way. Now, listen. I will give you a month—just a month—to tell the entire kingdom what you and your family have done.
Tell them about the killing of innocents, the families you have divided, and the torture you have brought upon people.
Tell them about who your son was and what you’ve done to ensure he died a scum.
Tell them everything, for after four weeks, if nothing of the sort happens, your entire family will be wiped out—and that includes everyone.
So, do well to do as I say. Also, your son hated you, by the way. I hope that makes you feel better.⟫
Kiel collapsed the moment he finished reading the note.
When he woke up, he was in bed, surrounded by a few doctors and elders of the family. They had obviously watched the video and read the note, so they knew what had caused this.
"Find him... *cough*... Find that bastard who killed my son and bring me his head!" Kiel shouted, coughing a few times.
"My lord, calm down first. We don’t know anything about this mysterious person. We need to take a step back here and fir—"
"I don’t care. Use whatever method you have to find him. I don’t care how much it will cost or how long it takes—just find him."
The elder who tried to speak kept quiet and simply bowed before leaving. Kiel, who had driven the elders away through his anger, passed out again.
It was clear he wasn’t going to heed Kent’s advice.
The room fell into a heavy silence after Kiel lost consciousness. The doctors exchanged uneasy glances while the remaining elders stood in solemn contemplation.
They were the trustworthy doctors of the Miller noble family, so they had seen and heard enough not to judge.
On the outside, however, the elders were not happy.
"We cannot afford to act recklessly. This enemy knows too much about us—our secrets, our weaknesses. If we charge blindly into this, we risk playing right into their hands," one of them said.
They knew nothing about Kent.
They didn’t know if this was a trap or not. But they knew something had to be done before it was too late.
"It’s obvious this is linked to the life Turyn was living. Now, it has come back to haunt us. The question, however, is which of his victims came back to hunt him—and us."

They were all aware of the kind of life Turyn had been living, yet they had said nothing to oppose him. Instead, they had stood by and watched as he destroyed families, friendships, and relationships, one after the other.
Now, they were at the short end of the stick, and it wasn’t looking good for them. If whoever this person was decided to come after them, they knew none of them would be spared.
This meant they had to do something about it, but none were willing to bend the knee or apologize to anyone.
They were the nobles, after all, not the other way around. Pride and arrogance had always been their shield, but now it felt more like a noose tightening around their necks.
The universe, ever observant, took notice of their predicament.
Thirty days were just around the corner, and the clock was ticking.

Meanwhile, the Malric Noble Family had just discovered that their son was murdered, along with his cohort. This sparked a chain of events that would soon lead them to learn of the same incident striking the Miller family.
Alliances had to be formed, but the question lingered: Would their family be the only ones facing this threat? Were they the only ones who had lived as scum and filth?

First, it was the Ashland Noble Family, wiped out without mercy. Then came the Alderford Merchant Family, slaughtered in a similar massacre. Now, the Malrics and the Millers were facing the same ominous fate.
The pattern was clear, and the message even clearer. Someone was targeting the corrupt, the powerful, and the unrepentant. The question was no longer *if* others would fall but *who* would be next.

chapters.title: Chapter 235: Long Overdue Revenge
paragraphs: "How did it go?" Kent asked, watching the expression on Alina’s face.
"It went well," Alina replied, but Kent could tell the expression on her face was that of shock. Obviously, talking with a literal god wasn’t something mere mortals could handle.
"She didn’t threaten you, right?" Kent asked, smiling.
"No, she did not. Big sister Vexthra is actually very sweet. I am just in shock and would need a few minutes to calm down if you don’t mind," Alina said, trying to calm her beating heart.
Kent just smiled, noticing how she had started calling her "big sister."
’It’s only natural; she is practically millions of years old.’
After calming down, Alina looked at Kent and said, "Big sister said you captured that bastard. Is it true?" she asked.
"Yes. I have him confined. Whenever you are ready, I can take you to him so you can exact your revenge," Kent responded.
"Good. I want to kill him now," Alina said, clenching her fist.
"Are you sure? Take a minute to think about it," Kent said. She had just been through a shocking moment; taking some time to calm down was always the way.
"I want to get it over with. I was weak all these years, and that was why he was able to live up to this moment. But now that I have him confined, I won’t let him keep living any longer."
"Okay then." Kent sighed. "Get dressed,"
Minutes later, they are fully dressed and ready.
Kent held her hand, and they vanished. They appeared in front of the Tower prison the next second. Alina turned around, looking at the place.
"Where are we?" she asked.
"We are inside my domain. It’s where I have everything under my control, including the lives of those inside," Kent answered, and Alina nodded.
"You are full of mysteries, Kent," she commented, still admiring the place.
"Don’t worry. After you finish what we came here to do, I will take you to where you will be spending most of your time."
He held her hand and gently led her through the prison, heading to the lower level where the miserable heir of the Miller family was currently waiting for his suffering to end.

"Remember, he is practically docile now, so you don’t have to worry about him. Just carry on with your revenge," Kent said, holding Alina’s hands. He then made sure she was okay before sending her to the prison cell.
"It’s you," Turyn said the moment they entered the prison. He had been under the torture blade of the Battle Doll for the past few days and instantly recognized Alina.
Kent raised an eyebrow.
"So, you remember me, huh?" Alina asked in a tone Kent could swear was amused. That was disturbing. It caused him to raise an eyebrow again.
"Please, let me go," Turyn pleaded, moving back. He didn’t have the strength to even stand, considering he hadn’t eaten for some time now.
"I said the same words to you a couple of years back, but your response was a slap in the face. Now you want me to let you go?" Alina said in a cold tone, making Kent raise another eyebrow.
"Please, let me go."
Alina wasn’t listening to any of that. She took out a dagger from her space ring and moved toward the trembling Turyn.
"You know, my mom was my everything. She was a mere maid, but she made sure I was cared for, and you took her from me. For this, I will kill you, so stop begging me."
She moved closer to him and, without any hesitation, drove her dagger through his eye. It was one swift and precise move without any hesitation or doubt.
She didn’t even look scared that she was about to take a life.
She stabbed forward, and the next second, Turyn breathed his last breath. He died just like that, and the pain she had carried all these years was finally vented.
[It’s shocking what hatred can do to a person,] Gaia said, making Kent nod.

Indeed, all this was hatred. Alina wasn’t some bloodthirsty fiend who held no value for human life. No, she was actually fragile. However, after accumulating this hatred for years, she had become numb to the pain Turyn was in.
This gave her the energy to do what she came there to do.
But now that she was done, Kent could only watch as the dagger in her hand fell to the ground and then her legs gave out.
He appeared behind her and caught her body.
She passed out.
Kent lifted her into a princess carry and vanished. The next second, she was sleeping on the large bed inside the harem tower.
Kent sighed and teleported back into the prison. He tapped into his Creator Necromancer class, and the gate opened. Turyn’s body vanished into it, and then it closed.
"That is my first human body. I want my undead to possess human bodies, so with this, I need beast corpses and some other resources to create quality undead."
[The master is indeed fortunate. Too bad the Pill Saint escaped death. Her poisoned body would have been a good material.]
"Indeed. She was fortunate. I just pray she comes after me again; that way, I will be able to kill her," Kent said, still recalling the events with the Pill Saint and her disciple.
Had it not been for Spear Saintess Neomi, she would have died, and he would have acquired a good body for creating his undead army.
"No worries, I will get another chance. I need to use the memory key right now," Kent sighed. "By the way, how does it work? Will I enter some sort of dream and relive these memories?"
[No. They will just flow into you. However, that is just for the memory keys. Some other ways will take a different turn, but those are for when you start remembering more of your past.]
"Okay then. I will handle that now so I can start my sword training. After the auction, I will go on my first mission, so I better prepare."

The next second, she was sleeping on the large bed inside the harem tower.
Kent sighed and teleported back into the prison.
He tapped into his Creator Necromancer class, and the gate opened.
Turyn’s body vanished into it, and then it closed.
"That is my first human body.
I want my undead to possess human bodies, so with this, I need beast corpses and some other resources to create quality undead."
[The master is indeed fortunate.
Too bad the Pill Saint escaped death.
Her poisoned body would have been a good material.]
"Indeed.
She was fortunate.
I just pray she comes after me again; that way, I will be able to kill her," Kent said, still recalling the events with the Pill Saint and her disciple.
Had it not been for Spear Saintess Neomi, she would have died, and he would have acquired a good body for creating his undead army.
"No worries, I will get another chance.
I need to use the memory key right now," Kent sighed.
"By the way, how does it work?
Will I enter some sort of dream and relive these memories?"
[No.
They will just flow into you.
However, that is just for the memory keys.
Some other ways will take a different turn, but those are for when you start remembering more of your past.]
"Okay then.
I will handle that now so I can start my sword training.
After the auction, I will go on my first mission, so I better prepare."

chapters.title: Chapter 236: The First Memory, Lord Genesis
paragraphs: Kent left for the Soul Tower, where he would be secluded to access and process the memories he would receive the moment he used the Memory Key.
He is a reincarnate, and for some unknown reason, he now has access to a way to regain his memories.
This, of course, wasn’t something that should be possible, simply because to undergo reincarnation, one has to forgo their previous memories.
In fact, having knowledge of your past self shouldn’t be possible.
What Kent went through when he was taken to Sonox was different. That was akin to transmigration under the authority of a god.
What he will be going through now is accessing an entirely different life. This shouldn’t be possible, yet he will be making it possible for unknown reasons.
Gaia and Akira are with him.
As they said, they want to know the kind of past Kent will be remembering. From their discussions, it was clear Kent has multiple past selves.
"Gaia, you said I won’t be going down memory lane, right?" Kent asked.
[Yes, Master. This is not a memory trip. This is just a key to open a small part of your past life. As to what and who you are, it will manifest the moment you see it.
I am no expert, so you might see something else, but fear not—this is a good thing... kinda.]
"Kinda?" Kent glared at the loli.
[No need to look so agitated, Master. The fact that you have a way to remember your past life is no simple thing. Not even gods can brag about that. So, cherish this.]
"Fine. But if something bad happens, I won’t ever use this key again," Kent sighed and then retrieved a key. He was standing outside the [Soul Pagoda].
⟪He really is going to do it. I can’t believe this moment has come.⟫ Akira said, looking ecstatic. It seemed she had been expecting this and was eager to see what would happen.
⟪No need to be so happy just yet. The key will open the memory door, but as to what he finds inside, we’ll never know.⟫ Gaia replied, though she wasn’t able to dampen Akira’s mood.
⟪Whatever... Still, I call dibs on the Dragon King.⟫
⟪You’re in for disappointment then. Master has already started walking the path of the sword, so no matter what, he will awaken Lord Genesis, the Savage sword.⟫
The two lolis continued their telepathic chitchat for a few minutes until Kent had enough and chose to use the key.
He pointed it forward and then twisted it. The moment he did, a wave of lightning burst out of the key. It was subtle and harmless but bloomed and soon formed into a door that slowly opened.
The moment it opened, a wave of familiar energy poured out from it, making Kent sigh inwardly. It was as if his life had finally found comfort and was calling out to him.
He turned to the two lolis. "I’ll be back the moment I’m done," he said to them before walking through the door without any hesitation.
Kent appeared in a small world filled with celestial energy when he walked through the door. The land was rich, and the plants were even richer.
It was as if he had entered the celestial realm, where only the primordial Celestial gods reside.
Well, that was exactly where he was. The place he had just appeared in was the Celestial Heavens. In all of the universe, only 13 beings have reached there...
One of them was the Dragon King, who died to save the universe during the Primordial Era.
The Dragon was the Primordial Chaos Dragon, and that dragon was Kent’s first self... his original self.

The realm he was in was the celestial world he had prepared with his three Anchors of the universe. Those three are Gaia, known as the Cosmic Weaver; Akira, the Soul Weaver; and Dori, the Mind Weaver.
This went way back. The beginning was as it should be, but it was also different. Kent would learn that later.
When the universe formed and life was born, the Primordial Chaos Dragon rose from the ashes of the burst eternal and spread his wings over everyone.
He was called the Guardian of the Universe, the Eternal Supreme, the Chaos Warden, and the Perverted Dragon King.
His supremacy captured the Universe’s attention, so he was chosen as the first and only son of the Universe. This meant he was given supremacy over the cycle of reincarnation.
This made him the only being who could reincarnate and remember his past lives.
But there was a catch.
As the son of the universe, he was bound to protect his mother. However, that wasn’t all. Before he became the son of the universe, he was promised 13 lives...
He would only have the chance to remember all 13 after he completed the cycle.
Thirteen lives came and went, and now, the cycle was complete. So, the promise made by the universe many billions of years ago was finally fulfilled.
The owner of the universe was now born and was about to walk through the 13 lives of rebirth. This was the promise made and the promise that had to be fulfilled.
’The one blessed by the power of reincarnation and rebirth is meant to wield all the power to protect what is sacred...’
"Thirteen Faceless Statues," Kent muttered as he gazed upward.
Thirteen large statues loomed above him, each with a staircase leading to it. They don’t have faces, but their presence is Supreme.
"I lived 13 lives. That’s a lot," Kent sighed. He gazed at the statues. One was a dragon, a swordsman, an assassin, an archer, a Spearman...
The 13 are all personifications of one aspect of his life. The Dragon was the first, but that was all. There was no description of them.
The Tower doesn’t have access to these, so Kent couldn’t learn anything about the statues.
"So, I get to pick where I want to go from here. That is simple, I guess." Kent moved toward the stair leading to the Swordsman.
The statue was holding a colossal sword with both hands, pointing the tip of the sword down. Kent could tell the sword was the same sword inside the Sword Tower.
He moved upward, and when he was in front of the statue, he saw a keyhole inside the sword. He looked at the key he was holding, which, for some reason, started fading.
He immediately knew what had to be done before it was too late. He placed it inside the hole and turned it...
A voice entered his head, and then he was sucked into the sword...
[Welcome, Lord Genesis. The Progenitor of the Sword Path.]

chapters.title: Chapter 237: Origin Story, The First Sword Path
paragraphs: Jest was an orphan, a slave, and a weakling.
Jest was the one you would feel pity for. His life was what one could describe as pitiful.
He was born in a slave mine. A few minutes after he was born, his mother was taken to carry out her duties. She was a slave miner, after all, so she ought to work.
No matter the situation you are in, you must work when your time has come. So she was taken away.
But she never returned.

That day, she was supposed to come back and hold her newborn in her arms, but she was buried alive by rubble, and her dream of caring for and someday scaling the Wall of Death with her son was lost in her final dream.
Her dream to make sure her son escaped the life of slavery was lost under the rubble.
Jest was then left to fend for himself as an infant.
Luckily, Auntie Ama was there, and she took care of him until he was 7 and could hold an axe. That was when he was branded and sent into the mine.
Welcome to the Mine of Alcatraz, the deepest and darkest mine to have ever existed in the world of Byrmrr.
Jest was just a boy who was born from an unjust union between a guard and a slave. He wasn’t meant to be born, but he was, and from the day he was born, he knew no happiness.

He was surrounded by horror, and so he had to adapt—and he did. He adapted and strived to live. He lived, and for 16 long years, Jest—or, as many slaves used to call him, the Daytime Dreamer—was a slave.
He was also a miner.
He was one of the hardworking slaves and one of the caring ones. His mother died, but she left him with a group of family members who loved him.
All slaves ought to stick together...
He was known as the daytime dreamer because he often dreamt of scaling the Wall of Death, the only way to escape the Mine. There, he would have to climb an 800-meter-tall wall.
If he fell, he would die.
Obviously, it was a lost cause, considering nobody had ever managed to scale it and escape the life they were living. Those who tried fell to their death.
Nobody had ever been able to do it.
But Jest was obsessed with the outside world. He was determined to learn, to grow, and one day live a peaceful life.
He doesn’t want to be a slave forever. No, he wants to change his destiny and become someone important.
Being a slave wasn’t something he asked for; it was what he was born into. So he wanted to escape that life.
And so it happened.
16 years later...exactly on the day he was born.
Jest went to the wall, looked up at the darkened skies filled with countless stars, and turned to his fellow slaves.
"Let it be known that today is when Jest scales the wall and escapes to claim his destiny."
He took his first step, the second, and the third until he was a quarter of the way up. Everyone watched with calm expressions.
They had seen countless people reach a quarter of the wall before.
But then he kept climbing until he was halfway up. Still, no one cheered, as this wasn’t new either. They had seen this happen every single day.
He moved to three-quarters of the wall, and everyone started shouting his name.
Morale was high. They wanted him to succeed. This was only the third time someone had reached 600 meters, and it had happened within two hours.
Jest was tired, but his determination kept pushing him. He kept moving, and before anyone could fully grasp how he was doing it, Jest was halfway there.
Then Jest climbed to 799 meters and looked down. He saw the faces of all the slaves, all of them with tears of joy falling down their faces. Some gave him the morale to go and live his life.
Most of the faces were those genuinely happy with what he had accomplished. They all wanted this and seeing one of them succeed; they were all happy for him.
He took ten whole minutes watching their expressions. After 10 minutes, a tear fell from his eyes, and he said with conviction,
"I will be back."
Jest climbed the last obstacle, and the dream he had was made a reality. He had escaped his life as a slave, and now, he could live a better life.
"Where to go... where to start..."
The question was a heavy one. He had no money...
Point of correction: he had a piece of stone, which he heard people call a spirit stone. Holding it filled his veins with energy. He also heard the elders call it money.
So he picked a direction and went.
He appeared in the city of orcs, where humans are treated as equals, for Byrmrr is a world of many races, and the humans and the orcs are allies.
He entered a store and bought clothes. He paid with the stone, and after 30 minutes, he was returned a sizable pouch of money as balance.
He left and, using his cleverness, managed to get to a human continent, which took him three months and half of his money.
He blended in.
Then, one day, he heard the phrase, "The Genesis Light Sect is recruiting mortals having the talent for cultivation."
That was all they said. But he went for it.
The minimum requirement was to have a Copper-grade spirit root.
The Genesis Light Sect recorded their 13th Platinum-grade spirit root disciple that day.
Jest was fortunate. He was a genius with a clean slate.
He was chosen by an Elder who was a swordsman, and since then, Jest started walking the path of the sword under the guidance of his master.
His cultivation talent was the best. He managed to rise through the ranks much faster, and his comprehension speed was also so great that within a couple of years, he became a Sword Grandmaster.
It was one of the best moments one could ask for. Jest was the person; he was the most talented. Even his master paled in comparison.
His talent with the sword was impeccable.

But the Sword Saint stage was the furthest he could go after five years. That was the extent of the knowledge available. The primitive sword path his master gave him could only take him to the Saint stage.
Rumour had it that the strongest path available could only go as far as the Sword King stage. So he was stuck.
His talent was being wasted. He tried for four more years, but he could not gain any form of understanding of how to progress.
So, he was depressed and didn’t know how to move forward.

Until he said to himself, "I will create my own path, and just like how I scaled the wall of death, I will take this to the peak. I will name it the Genesis Sword Path, for this will be the first path to the pinnacle of the Sword Dao."
Kent woke up inside the Tower feeling different...

chapters.title: Chapter 238: The Memory Effect
paragraphs: Kent woke up sweating.
He was now inside the Sword Gate, surrounded by the two lolis, Gaia and Akira.
"What happened?" he asked calmly, but the mood and aura around him were different. Gaia was happy, and Akira was not smiling, though she was happy.
She predicted Kent would remember his life as the Chaos Dragon, but from the sharp aura around him, it was no secret he had just returned from the memory of him as a swordsman.
"One minute, you entered the door; the next, you appeared here. It was a couple of seconds at best," Gaia said, making Kent raise an eyebrow.
"A couple of seconds?" he asked.
"Yes, Master. You entered, and before we knew it, you were back inside the Sword Gate. It all happened so fast," Akira answered this time, making Kent sigh.
’I was there for a couple of minutes...At least that is what I remember.’ He said to himself
He stood up and walked toward the Sword of Enlightenment.
’It’s the same sword as the one in that weird place,’ he said. He then turns to the two Loli’s beside him
"I will need the next few days to cultivate. Notify me if something happens while I am here," Kent said before sitting in a lotus posture.

With his authority inside the tower, he could tell Alina was still not awake. But he wasn’t about to worry about that, considering she wouldn’t have any visitors in the outside world for the next couple of days.
She can sleep for a month, and only two days will pass in the outside world.
The two lolis left despite having so many questions. They knew what had to be done, so they left to give Kent the time to handle his affairs.
"So, I was just a slave and a dreamer, huh?" A small smirk appeared on his face as he went through the memories.
It was from when he was born up to when he declared that he would create his own sword path—the first sword path.
He was a slave for 16 good years. Then, he escaped under the watchful eyes of all the guards. They didn’t stop him, mainly because that was the way out created for all the slaves.
Afterwards, he joined a sect and was picked by a swordsman who became his master and taught him the path of the sword. He was a quick study, though the path back then wasn’t up to the standards.
"I have so many questions, like how did they know the Saint stage was the last for that path? Or wait, how did anyone know the path goes beyond the Sword King stage?"
He asked himself, but the answer came faster than expected.
"The Sword Dao"
The Daos are the paths set by nature. They are simply there. You don’t need to find a predetermined path to follow if you have what it takes to find your way.
The path is essentially about finding your own way to comprehend the Dao.
That was what Kent, as Jest, discovered. He knew that there had to be a way to keep moving, so he created a way to keep moving.
"I was a genius," he smiled and extended his hand for his sword to appear. He stood up and drew his sword from its sheath, causing a powerful energy to engulf him entirely.
His sword intent and qi burst out; now, they appear more refined and deadly.
"As anticipated, the memories are like me reliving my life as Jest. My understanding of the sword has clearly improved, and it was because of Jest."
He smiled as he remembered how he would sit down after his shift in the mines and gaze at the tall wall. He could now remember clearly how it felt when he was halfway there.
’I was determined, focused, and brilliant back then. I need to be even more remarkable this time, considering I can learn and improve from my mistakes.’
Kent was rather very happy to have remembered that part of his past.
He was drawing closer to the Profound Sword Intent and Qi stage, and it was all thanks to his past as Jest. Now, he had a much deeper understanding of the basics of the sword.
This influenced not only his understanding but also the way he used his aura.
"I guess there is no better time than now to start practising for the Sword Saint stage. Who knows when the next set of memories will be given to me."
He looked at the [Sword of Enlightenment] and sheathed his sword. He sat in a lotus posture and began comprehending the next 10,002 sword moves.

This time, he was using his mind instead of picking up his sword to practice. It was because he needed to train his mind to focus so that when he picked up the sword, no matter the situation, he could remain focused.
It was one of the many aspects every swordsman should have. Their focus should always be on the sword in their hands.
And to achieve that, they must train their minds.

Just like that, three days passed inside the tower, but Kent didn’t even move a finger. His eyes were closed, and the only things changing about him for the past three days were his sword aura and intent.
His presence was becoming much sharper and more refined.
It was as if he finally understood what a swordsman should be like. He spent two days going through Jest’s memories, which helped him come to terms with his path as a swordsman.

sentences.text: Kent woke up sweating.
He was now inside the Sword Gate, surrounded by the two lolis, Gaia and Akira.
"What happened?" he asked calmly, but the mood and aura around him were different.
Gaia was happy, and Akira was not smiling, though she was happy.
She predicted Kent would remember his life as the Chaos Dragon, but from the sharp aura around him, it was no secret he had just returned from the memory of him as a swordsman.
"One minute, you entered the door; the next, you appeared here.
It was a couple of seconds at best," Gaia said, making Kent raise an eyebrow.
"A couple of seconds?" he asked.
"Yes, Master.
You entered, and before we knew it, you were back inside the Sword Gate.
It all happened so fast," Akira answered this time, making Kent sigh.
’I was there for a couple of minutes...At least that is what I remember.’ He said to himself
He stood up and walked toward the Sword of Enlightenment.
’It’s the same sword as the one in that weird place,’ he said.
He then turns to the two Loli’s beside him
"I will need the next few days to cultivate.
Notify me if something happens while I am here," Kent said before sitting in a lotus posture.
With his authority inside the tower, he could tell Alina was still not awake.
But he wasn’t about to worry about that, considering she wouldn’t have any visitors in the outside world for the next couple of days.
She can sleep for a month, and only two days will pass in the outside world.
The two lolis left despite having so many questions.
They knew what had to be done, so they left to give Kent the time to handle his affairs.
"So, I was just a slave and a dreamer, huh?" A small smirk appeared on his face as he went through the memories.
It was from when he was born up to when he declared that he would create his own sword path—the first sword path.
He was a slave for 16 good years.
Then, he escaped under the watchful eyes of all the guards.
They didn’t stop him, mainly because that was the way out created for all the slaves.
Afterwards, he joined a sect and was picked by a swordsman who became his master and taught him the path of the sword.
He was a quick study, though the path back then wasn’t up to the standards.
"I have so many questions, like how did they know the Saint stage was the last for that path?
Or wait, how did anyone know the path goes beyond the Sword King stage?"
He asked himself, but the answer came faster than expected.
"The Sword Dao"
The Daos are the paths set by nature.
They are simply there.
You don’t need to find a predetermined path to follow if you have what it takes to find your way.
The path is essentially about finding your own way to comprehend the Dao.
That was what Kent, as Jest, discovered.
He knew that there had to be a way to keep moving, so he created a way to keep moving.

His sword intent and qi burst out; now, they appear more refined and deadly.

He could now remember clearly how it felt when he was halfway there.
’I was determined, focused, and brilliant back then.

Kent was rather very happy to have remembered that part of his past.
He was drawing closer to the Profound Sword Intent and Qi stage, and it was all thanks to his past as Jest.
Now, he had a much deeper understanding of the basics of the sword.
This influenced not only his understanding but also the way he used his aura.

It was one of the many aspects every swordsman should have.
Their focus should always be on the sword in their hands.
And to achieve that, they must train their minds.
